items.title: Ycrystal
items.text:
Ycrystal is a desktop application for Linux, macOS, and Windows for composing crystal-structure figures and rendering the current view with POV-Ray. The live interface uses PySide6 and VTK; the exported scene keeps the same orthographic camera and displayed atoms.

Early development. You can open POSCAR/CONTCAR, CIF, and Quantum ESPRESSO inputs (any ibrav), save self-contained .ycrystal projects, navigate, select and hide individual displayed atoms, export scenes, and render PNG, PDF, or JPEG figures. Supercell repetitions, periodic bonds, cell-edge modes, and view-direction controls are available, as are an output frame, a POV-Ray preview, cancellable renders, and galleries of 30 materials and 12 environments with POV-Ray thumbnails, per-element and per-atom materials, floors, skies, and lighting controls, and an element legend for the figure. Drag the a/b/c handles to add cells, rotate freely or about a lattice/Cartesian axis, and reuse a figure's style with another structure, in the window or from the command line; every figure change is undoable.

Ycrystal 0.5.0 includes the element legend and support for Quantum ESPRESSO ibrav other than 0 in both the Windows installer and tagged source. These pages follow main. See the release and feature status for details.

  • Install and launch on Linux Mint or macOS.
  • Follow Your first crystal figure using the built-in SrTiO3 sample.
  • Find controls, supported formats, and rendering instructions; save a figure with a self-contained snapshot and a provenance record for reproducible figures.
  • Read the architecture, try the Python examples, or consult the API reference.
  • See troubleshooting and limitations and the progress record and roadmap for the current scope and evidence.

This is an actual 640 × 400 POV-Ray render, generated from Ycrystal's shared scene and default camera. The live viewport uses approximate lighting and also shows orientation axes. Regenerate the image.

The Python interfaces are evolving developer functionality. They do not currently carry a stable public API guarantee. This site is built from the repository and published at ymatterlab.github.io/ycrystal.

items.title: Supported file formats
items.text:
Ycrystal opens structure files and its own project files with File ▸ Open… (Ctrl+O) or from the command line: ycrystal FILE [--format poscar|cif|qe|project]. The format is detected from the file name and content. If it cannot be determined, Ycrystal asks; File ▸ Open As… (or --format) sets it explicitly. A file that cannot be read leaves the current scene unchanged and shows the reason.

The same summary is available in the application under Help ▸ Supported File Formats.

items.title: VASP POSCAR / CONTCAR
items.text:
Recognised names: POSCAR*, CONTCAR*, *.vasp, *.poscar, or POSCAR-like content.

Supported:

  • VASP 5 files (element line) and VASP 4 files (no element line).
  • Direct or Cartesian coordinates; one or three scale factors; a negative scale factor is the cell volume in Å³.
  • Selective dynamics: kept per atom and axis, shown in the selection information (fixed x y z or free) and saved in projects.
  • Any cell shape.

VASP 4 files carry no element names. Ycrystal does not guess them from the comment line (a comment such as "In plane strained GaN" would otherwise read as In and Ga). It asks for the element of each species in the order of the atom counts and proposes symbols only when the comment lists exactly element symbols.

items.title: CIF
items.text:
Recognised names: *.cif, or content with data_ and _cell_length_a.

Supported:

  • Symmetry expansion from the listed symmetry operations or the space-group symbol.
  • Any cell shape; the lattice is oriented with a along x and b in the xy plane.
  • Several data blocks: Ycrystal asks which structure to open.
  • Site labels (e.g. Fe1) are kept separately from elements; occupancies are recorded.

Not supported (the file is rejected with an explanation):

  • Partially occupied or mixed sites (numeric _atom_site_occupancy below 1 - 1e-3; near-unit values within this tolerance are retained).
  • Distinct sites at the same position.

Ycrystal draws ordered structures only and never shows a disordered structure as if it were ordered. Use an ordered model with explicit atoms instead.

items.title: Quantum ESPRESSO pw.x input
items.text:
Recognised names: *.in, *.pwi, pw.in, pwscf.in, or content with &SYSTEM and ATOMIC_POSITIONS.

Supported:

  • ibrav = 0 with a CELL_PARAMETERS card in alat, bohr, or angstrom units. alat uses celldm(1) (bohr) or A (Å).
  • Every other ibrav of pw.x: 1, 2, 3, −3, 4, 5, −5, 6, 7, 8, 9, −9, 91, 10, 11, 12, −12, 13, −13, and 14, with the lattice given by celldm(1)…celldm(6) or by A, B, C, cosAB, cosAC, cosBC. Ycrystal builds the same lattice vectors as pw.x (QE 6.5 and later), so crystal coordinates mean the same thing; alat positions use a. The parameters are checked as pw.x checks them. Files with ibrav = −13 and crystal positions written for QE 6.4.1 or older need converting. The vectors of every lattice, the parameters each needs, the refused inputs, the dependence on the QE version, and how this was verified are in Quantum ESPRESSO lattices.
  • ATOMIC_POSITIONS in alat, bohr, angstrom, or crystal units. Each coordinate may be simple arithmetic, as pw.x allows: numbers, +, -, *, /, ^ (power), and parentheses, without spaces (for example 1/4, 2*(1/8), -2^2 = −4). ^ and signs bind tightest and group from the right, then * and /, then + and -.
  • Numbers in Fortran notation, such as 16.D0 or 1.5d-3, in the namelists and in the ATOMIC_SPECIES, CELL_PARAMETERS, and ATOMIC_POSITIONS cards.
  • Species labels such as Fe1, Fe_up, or O-2 (an element symbol followed by a digit, _, -, +, or .). Labels are kept; the element is taken from the label.
  • if_pos flags (0/1 after the coordinates), kept like selective dynamics.

Not supported (the file is rejected with an explanation):

  • A CELL_PARAMETERS card together with an ibrav other than 0 (pw.x refuses it as redundant too).
  • ATOMIC_POSITIONS crystal_sg (symmetry-reduced positions).
  • A coordinate that pw.x's arithmetic cannot evaluate (1/0, an unbalanced parenthesis); the message names the line.

Labels that do not name an element unambiguously (for example Cb, which could be carbon) require the element to be entered when opening. Ycrystal never runs pw.x and does not need pseudopotential files.

items.title: Ycrystal projects (.ycrystal)
items.text:
File ▸ Save Project (Ctrl+S) writes a versioned JSON file with:

  • the complete structure (cell, positions, elements, labels, occupancies, movable flags),
  • where it came from (original path and name, format, SHA-256 checksum, data block, element mapping, import time, reader version),
  • display settings (repetitions, cell edges, boundary atoms, hidden atoms, bond rules, atom size and element radii), materials (default, element, and atom overrides), element colours, and the environment (background, floor, lighting),
  • the camera of the output image and the output size.

A project reopens without the original structure file and reproduces the coordinates exactly. Closing or opening another file with unsaved changes (including a changed view) asks whether to save, discard, or cancel.

The camera is stored for the explicit output size, so a project reopens with the same framing in a window of any shape.

Current project schema is 8 (schema 6 added background pictures, stored in ZIP packages, and custom material definitions; schema 7 added atom-attached vectors; schema 8 added the element legend, scene.legend). Older projects remain readable with their original appearance and no legend (schema-1 projects load with bonds switched off, as they were drawn). Newer schemas are rejected with a message to update Ycrystal.

items.title: Figure snapshots and provenance records
items.text: ycrystal FILE … --render OUT.png --save-project FIGURE.ycrystal (and "save_projects": true in a batch manifest) saves the rendered figure as an ordinary project, the snapshot, with the camera and output size it was rendered with, and a JSON provenance record FIGURE.provenance.json (format: ycrystal-provenance, schema 1) with the versions, settings, and SHA-256 checksums of the input, style, snapshot, and image. In a snapshot the structure's import record has no path (the original folder); its name, format, and checksum remain. See reproducible figures.

items.title: Ycrystal styles (.ycstyle)
items.text: File ▸ Export Style… writes the presentation without structure and camera: materials, colours, radii, the element legend, display settings, the environment, the output size, and the element sequence of the source structure (used to decide whether per-atom settings can transfer). See reusing the look for the transfer rules. Style files are versioned JSON, or a ZIP package when they carry a background picture; newer versions are rejected (style schema 3 added the element legend; older styles load without one). An element mapping chosen when a style is applied (element mapping) is not stored in the style file, which stays unchanged; a project saved afterwards stores the resulting element settings.

items.title: Development handoff
items.text:
The state of Ycrystal for continuing work on another machine: the Linux Mint laptop, the office Mac mini, or the Windows 11 laptop. Rules for Claude Code are in CLAUDE.md at the repository root; the detailed verification record is PROGRESS.md.

This file records state. It does not authorize work: implement only what the user asks for in the current task (see the rules at the end).

items.title: Current project status
items.text:
• Ycrystal 0.5.0 includes the element legend (PR #45) and expanded Quantum ESPRESSO reader (PR #47). The Windows installer and tagged source are listed on the release page. This website follows development on main. See the release checklist for verification.
  • Documentation published (22 November 2026): the generated gh-pages branch serves ymatterlab.github.io/ycrystal. GitHub Pages uses that branch's root, with HTTPS enforced. The publishing workflow was merged into main in PR #48. See the publication record.
  • FR-QE-IBRAV-01, Quantum ESPRESSO input with ibrav other than 0: merged in PR #47 on 21 November 2026 (merge commit c2fa44a), after v0.4.0. Supports all 20 lattices of pw.x, checked against pw.x's own output (17 lattices, 295 inputs of QE's test suite) and the pw.x documentation (all 20); Fortran numbers (16.D0) in cards and arithmetic in positions (1/4) read as pw.x reads them. User guide page docs/guide/qe-lattices.md. Verified on the Linux laptop and in CI on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows; opening these files by hand remains unchecked. See PROGRESS.md.
  • FR-LEGEND-01, element legend (requested 21 November 2026): merged in PR #45 (merge commit 6735400) after CI passed on every system. A Scene ▸ Legend tab and a legend of the displayed elements painted onto the figure, its previews, renders, and exports (project schema 8, style schema 3). Included in v0.5.0. See PROGRESS.md.
  • Windows support (requested by the user on 17 November 2026), branch feature/windows, PR #35: completed on a Windows 11 laptop on 18 November 2026. All automated tests pass there with POV-Ray for Windows, and the user tested Ycrystal by hand and reports that it works well. PR #35 was merged after CI passed (merge commit ae01f43). PR #36 (branch ci/windows-povray) makes Windows CI render with the real POV-Ray for Windows, installed from the ci-assets release (see docs/development/windows-port.md); merged. PR #39, branch feature/windows-install (the user's request for a simpler Windows installation): scripts\install-windows.ps1, a Start-menu entry and .ycrystal file type through --install-desktop, and POV-Ray's editor question reported instead of waited for (see windows-port.md). Merged before: FR-STYLE-CLI-01 (PR #28), FR-STYLE-MAP-01 (PR #29), FR-CAMERA-01 (PR #30), FR-BATCH-01 (PR #31), FR-REPRO-01 (PR #32; the user tested it by hand), FR-VALIDATION-01 (PR #33), and FR-GALLERY-01 with the next-tests audit (PR #34, merge commit 5b72f92). All of this work is included in v0.4.0.

The table gives the first release tag containing each feature. v0.5.0 includes the features from earlier releases. GitHub release pages for v0.4.0 and v0.5.0 provide Windows installers.

First release tag / availability Feature Merged 0.1.0 Milestones M0–M6: import, projects, navigation, selection, supercells, bonds, materials, environments, previews, rendering, styles, desktop launcher tag v0.1.0 0.2.0 FR-COLOR-01 colour dialog and names; FR-RENDER-01 aspect-ratio lock; FR-LIGHT-01 Lighting Setup window and live lighting PRs #13–#15, tag v0.2.0 0.3.0 FR-MEASURE-01 distance and bond-angle measurements (Measurements panel) PR #16 0.3.0 FR-PREVIEW-01 adjustable POV-Ray preview resolution PR #17 0.3.0 FR-BGIMAGE-01 background pictures, ZIP project/style packages (project schema 6) PR #18 0.3.0 FR-MATERIAL-01 custom material variants (Customize Material…, personal materials) PR #18 0.3.0 FR-VECTOR-01 atom-attached direction/magnetic-moment vectors (project schema 7) PR #19 0.3.0 Maintenance: macOS (Apple silicon) support, Ubuntu + macOS CI PR #22, tag v0.3.0 0.4.0 FR-EXPORT-01 PNG/PDF/JPEG export, publication size presets, custom size and dpi PR #23 0.4.0 Maintenance: new application icon and logo, logo-rendering script; Linux launcher refreshes the icon cache PRs #25, #26 0.4.0 FR-STYLE-CLI-01 --style/--style-parts apply a .ycstyle before --render/--export-pov PR #28 0.4.0 FR-STYLE-MAP-01 element mapping for styles (--element-map, Import Style dialog) PR #29 0.4.0 FR-CAMERA-01 --view, --camera-policy, --fit-margin, --view-height (shared with View along) PR #30 0.4.0 FR-BATCH-01 --batch MANIFEST --output-dir DIR (--dry-run, --overwrite), report JSON PR #31 0.4.0 FR-REPRO-01 --save-project FIGURE.ycrystal, manifest save_projects, provenance records PR #32 0.4.0 FR-VALIDATION-01 validation tests, scripts/benchmark_render.py, scripts/replay_check.py, evidence report (no application change) PR #33 0.4.0 FR-GALLERY-01 publication gallery (examples/publication/, scripts/make_gallery.py), gallery and manuscript-figure pages (no application change) PR #34 0.4.0 Maintenance: Windows 11 support with POV-Ray for Windows 3.7 (no FR ID) PR #35 (ae01f43) 0.4.0 Maintenance: Windows CI with the real POV-Ray for Windows (ci-assets release) PR #36 (8051f04) 0.4.0 Graphical Windows installer (PyInstaller + Inno Setup), coexisting with the developer installation (no FR ID) PR #40 (2f427ac) 0.4.0 Maintenance: Windows installation script, Start-menu entry and .ycrystal file type (--install-desktop on Windows), editor question reported (no FR ID) PR #39 0.4.0 Python 3.12–3.14 support; Python 3.13 verified on macOS and Python 3.13/3.14 on Windows PRs #38, #39 0.5.0 FR-QE-IBRAV-01 QE input with ibrav other than 0 (all pw.x lattices) PR #47 (c2fa44a) 0.5.0 FR-LEGEND-01 element legend: Legend tab, live overlay, legend painted onto previews, renders, and PNG/PDF/JPEG exports; project schema 8, style schema 3 PR #45 (6735400)

Each has automated checks recorded in PROGRESS.md. Hands-on checks by a person are still open for most of them; the user reports FR-VECTOR-01, FR-EXPORT-01, and FR-REPRO-01 working, and Ycrystal on Windows working well.

Known limitations and unresolved issues:

  • Background pictures show only their average colour in the live VTK view; there is no rename/delete UI for personal materials; live-view speed with thousands of vector arrows is unmeasured; the Lighting Setup overview does not draw vector arrows.
  • macOS: Ycrystal runs from the source checkout. There is no application bundle, so the Dock and the menu bar show "Python", and .ycrystal files do not open by double click.
  • macOS: nothing has been checked by hand yet, and no Retina display was available (see Cross-platform status).
  • Windows: Ycrystal runs from the source checkout, installed by scripts\install-windows.ps1 and started from the Start menu (or .venv\Scripts\ycrystal.exe). POV-Ray for Windows renders one copy at a time (Ycrystal reports a copy the user has open), reports no progress percentage, and takes the keyboard focus during renders started from a terminal. POV-Ray for Windows shows its About box at its second start and then every 14 days; renders wait until the user clicks OK (documented; Ycrystal changes no POV-Ray setting). Its question about a missing editor at every start is now reported by Ycrystal instead of waited for. Rendering with a %TEMP% path outside a legacy code page (for example a Chinese user name on a Western-European Windows) is unverified.
  • FR-EXPORT-01: the PDF holds the POV-Ray raster image (not vector graphics); PDF page sizes are whole points (up to 0.18 mm from the exact size); JPEG fills a transparent background with white. Not yet run on Linux or checked by hand.
  • FR-REPRO-01: pixel differences of snapshot replays between systems or POV-Ray builds are unmeasured (same machine: identical pixels, never identical PNG bytes); not run on macOS; snapshots only for PNG renders from the command line.
  • FR-VALIDATION-01: everything was measured on the Linux laptop only. Not run: the benchmark and the validation tests on the Mac, the full benchmark set (too heavy for the laptop), and replays between two machines (commands in docs/development/validation.md). The comparison with VESTA, OVITO, and CView is from their documentation only. No independent evaluation has taken place.
  • FR-GALLERY-01: the gallery was rendered on the Linux laptop only. Its snapshots have not been replayed on another machine. Figure 1 (schematic, screenshot) and the plots of Figure 4 are still to be made (docs/development/manuscript-figures.md).
  • JAC submission: referees need anonymous access to the program and a web page with documentation (per the journal's instructions; recheck them). The repository is now public, so the program can be cloned without an account; the documentation website is now published.
  • Found during FR-REPRO-01, not changed: save_project (and so every project and snapshot) is written through mkstemp and ends up readable by the owner only (mode 0600 on Linux/macOS), which matters for shared folders. The new provenance records behave the same. Decide whether to change it (a separate task).

items.title: Latest development session
items.text:
• Date and machine: 21 November 2026, the Linux Mint laptop (Python 3.12.3, PySide6 6.12.0, VTK 9.7.2, POV-Ray 3.7.0.10; no Xvfb installed, so GUI tests opened windows on the desktop).
  • Done first: the copyright holder and author changed from "Y-Matter Lab" to the owner's name in the licence, package metadata, README, and Windows installer metadata (PR #44, merged at 844775d). The QSettings organisation name and data folders stay "Y-Matter Lab" on purpose, so existing settings keep working.
  • Then: FR-LEGEND-01 on feature/element-legend, PR #45 (details and evidence in PROGRESS.md). The legend is a 2D layer painted with Qt onto the rendered PNG in finish_job; the live view draws the same layout as an overlay; Fit keeps the structure beside it.
  • Then: the first CI run of PR #45 failed on Windows only: QImageWriter keeps its output file open until it is destroyed, so the legend's temporary PNG could not be renamed over the image ("being used by another process"). Fixed by encoding into a QBuffer (ee6f04a); CI then passed everywhere (run 44911218624: Ubuntu 963 passed, 10 skipped on each of Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14; macOS 781 passed, 10 skipped; Windows 789 passed, 2 skipped, with POV-Ray for Windows; docs, pre-commit, Windows installer). Merged at 6735400, as the user asked.
  • Not done: hands-on use of the Legend tab on any system; GUI tests on macOS and Windows (CI runs only the tests without windows there).
  • Then: FR-QE-IBRAV-01 on feature/qe-ibrav (details in PROGRESS.md). ASE 3.29 does not read ibrav ≠ 0; the utils/ function is ASE 3.22.1's old ibrav_to_cell (LGPL), so it served as a cross-check, and Ycrystal has its own implementation from the pw.x documentation. An audit of every ibrav added a reader test for all 20 lattices in both forms and compared 289 inputs of QE's test suite with pw.x's output (all agree); −9, 91, −13 have no pw.x reference in QE. Then, at the user's request, Fortran numbers (16.D0) in cards and arithmetic in positions (1/4) are read as pw.x reads them; 295 of 295 QE inputs agree. Full suite 1115 passed, 10 skipped (Windows-only). Subsequently committed, pushed, and merged in PR #47 (c2fa44a) after CI passed on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows. Not done: opening such a file in the window by hand.

Earlier, on 18 November 2026:

  • Date and machine: 18 November 2026, a Windows 11 laptop (x64, 125 % display scale, Python 3.12.10 from python.org, POV-Ray for Windows 3.7.0 from the official installer).
  • Done: the Windows port on feature/windows, continuing PR #35 (summary in PROGRESS.md, details in windows-port.md):
  • experiments with the real POV-Ray for Windows answered the takeover's ten questions; its source code (GitHub, 3.7-stable) explained the single-instance and command-line rules;
  • it takes the keyboard focus (now held by the window while it runs) and keeps a single instance (now checked first and explained; Ycrystal's own renders take turns);
  • the window's renders of POV-Ray for Windows run through subprocess.Popen, since PySide6's QProcess cannot start a program minimised;
  • include files and settings found through the registry's DocPath; taskbar identity and an .exe filter for the executable dialog;
  • a bug of the new process backend (renders waiting for ever after a window closed mid-render) found by the GUI tests and fixed, with a regression test.
  • Then: the user tested Ycrystal by hand on the laptop ("it works well") and asked for a documentation audit (Windows commands name ycrystal.exe and python.exe; the py launcher needs a terminal opened after Python's installation), a commit, and the merge of PR #35 once CI passes. CI passed (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, docs, pre-commit) after one test fix (metals.inc exists in Ubuntu's system include folder); merged at ae01f43.
  • Then (PR #36): the user chose to keep the official POV-Ray for Windows installer as an asset of a ci-assets release (povray.org blocks CI downloads). Screenshots taken by the probe on the runner showed two POV-Ray dialogs that wait even with /EXIT (the editor question; the About box from the second start on); the job now pre-sets UseEditors=0 and ItsAboutTime. The Windows job is no longer experimental: 727 passed, 2 skipped (POSIX-only), with YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1.

items.title: Next recommended steps
items.text:
• FR-QE-IBRAV-01 (merged in PR #47; CI passed): run scripts/check_qe_ibrav.py once on the Mac and on Windows (docs/development/next-tests.md, step 1f); open an ibrav file in the window by hand (for example tests/fixtures/Si_ibrav2.pw.in).

  • FR-LEGEND-01 (merged in PR #45): a hands-on check of the Legend tab on Linux, the Mac, and Windows: switch the legend on, Fit, try each position, layout, font, and order, render PNG/PDF/JPEG, and compare the image with the frame; run the GUI legend tests (tests/test_gui_legend.py) on the Mac and on Windows.

  • On the Mac mini, first: git checkout main && git pull. PR #36 is already merged and included in v0.4.0. Reinstall into the existing .venv (.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e ".[dev]" -c constraints.txt; no dependency changed) and run the full suite with real windows (use current CI results for expected counts). The Windows changes keep povray on macOS on the same QProcess path as before, but nothing of them has run on a real Mac yet.

  • Windows, later: a fuller hands-on check on a second Windows computer when one is available; decide whether Ycrystal should notice POV-Ray for Windows' About box (see windows-port.md).
  • Run the tests of docs/development/next-tests.md (audited 17 November 2026, counts updated 18 November), in its order:
  • on the Mac mini: the full suite with real windows (use current CI results for expected counts), the memory check, the benchmark, replays of the Linux reference sets, and the gallery;
  • by hand on the Mac and the laptop;
  • a clean-computer dry run.

Record results only as they are obtained. 4. For the manuscript: draw the workflow schematic and take the window screenshot (Figure 1), make the plots of Figure 4 from the recorded data, and have two independent evaluators work through the checklist. 5. Try the mapping rows of the Import Style dialog by hand once (only scripted GUI checks so far), for example with tests/fixtures/BaZrO3.cif and examples/grey-studio.ycstyle as in the examples guide; and the View along buttons in every order (the camera fix of PR #30). 6. Watch CI for an intermittent failure: one local full run of PR #30's suite reported 1 failure that did not reproduce (PR #30's CI and three later full runs passed); its name was not captured. 7. Optional check (no new work): place an exported PDF in a LaTeX or Word document and check its size there.

Every request of the private plan's section 15 is now merged or in review. Nothing further is authorized by this record; new work needs its own request.

Still open from the macOS task: the hands-on macOS checklist.

Suggestions only — not approved, ask before starting any of them:

  • FR-LEGEND-01 follow-ups: dragging the legend in the view; a --legend command-line option (today the legend comes from a project or style); a picture of the legend in the user guide.

  • A command-line option for PDF/JPEG (--render figure.pdf --dpi 600); the CLI still writes PNG only.

  • A macOS application bundle or launcher (name and icon in the Dock, opening .ycrystal files from Finder).
  • Windows: progress percentages from POV-Ray for Windows' window title (see windows-port.md); code signing of the graphical installer (needs a certificate); attaching the installer to the next release (release procedure, step 5).
  • From earlier sessions: hide the disabled Bottom/Clouds rows for the Image background type; a way to manage personal materials; hands-on checks of the unreleased features, then the next release (FR-EXPORT-01 and the branding): move the changelog's "Unreleased" section under a version, bump __version__, and run the checklist in docs/development/release.md before tagging, when the user decides.

Dependencies and blockers:

  • The repository is public, so GitHub's standard hosted runners, macOS included, cost nothing. If it became private again, macOS minutes would be billed at a higher rate than Linux minutes; then restrict the macOS job (for example to main and manual runs).
  • GitHub's hosted Macs have no GPU, so the GUI tests cannot run there reliably; they need a real Mac.
  • Windows: POV-Ray for Windows is a GUI program without a povray command. Ycrystal drives pvengine64.exe with /EXIT /NR +GAscene.log scene.ini (PR #35); confirmed on a Windows 11 laptop on 18 November 2026. It cannot render while a copy of it is open with Keep Single Instance on (its default); Ycrystal says so.

items.title: Hands-on checks on a Mac
items.text:
Automated tests cannot establish these. Start with .venv/bin/ycrystal --sample perovskite and note what fails.

  • [ ] The window opens, the structure is drawn sharply, and it fills the whole view (on a Retina display: not a quarter of it, not blurred).
  • [ ] Mouse: left drag orbits, Shift + left drag pans, right drag and the wheel zoom. Trackpad: two-finger scrolling zooms at a usable speed; pinching zooms.
  • [ ] Click selects the atom under the cursor (also on a Retina display); ⌘ + click toggles; Delete (⌫) hides; Esc clears.
  • [ ] Menus: Ycrystal's Quit is in the application menu; ⌘O, ⌘S, ⇧⌘S, ⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z, ⌘R, ⌘M, ⌘← / ⌘→, F (Fit), and F5 (Preview; may need Fn) work with the 3D view focused.
  • [ ] File dialogs: Open lists POSCAR/CONTCAR files without an extension, .cif, .pw.in; Save Project adds .ycrystal; Render Image… (PNG, PDF, JPEG) and Export POV-Ray… save.
  • [ ] Render ▸ Set POV-Ray Executable… starts in the folder of the found executable; Render ▸ Check Renderer passes.
  • [ ] Preview with Update automatically on: one preview per change, no repeated re-rendering while idle, also in a small window.
  • [ ] Supercell handles, measurement modes, Lighting Setup window (drag the key light), Vectors window, Customize Material… (saving a personal material creates its thumbnail), background picture.
  • [ ] Appearance: readable in macOS dark mode; colour dialog and galleries.
  • [ ] A long render can be cancelled; closing the window during a render exits cleanly.
  • [ ] A project saved on Linux opens on the Mac and renders the same image, and the reverse.

items.title: Development environment notes
items.text:
Common to all systems: one virtual environment per machine and per checkout (.venv; .venv-docs for the documentation). A virtual environment copied from another operating system does not work: recreate it with python3.12 -m venv --clear .venv.

Linux Mint 22 / Ubuntu 24.04:

sudo apt install git povray povray-includes libxcb-cursor0 python3.12-venv
/usr/bin/python3 -m venv .venv          # the system Python, not Conda

macOS (Homebrew; verified on macOS 15.8, Apple silicon):

xcode-select --install                  # Git and command-line tools, if missing
brew install python@3.12 povray         # POV-Ray 3.7 with its include files
python3.12 -m venv .venv

Then, on either system, from the repository root:

.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e ".[dev]" -c constraints.txt
.venv/bin/ycrystal --version            # ycrystal 0.5.0
.venv/bin/ycrystal --check-renderer     # PASS: POV-Ray 3.7… passed
.venv/bin/ycrystal --sample perovskite  # opens the window
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -rs       # GUI tests open windows for about 1.5 minutes
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --all-files
python3.12 -m venv .venv-docs && .venv-docs/bin/python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
.venv-docs/bin/zensical build --clean --strict

POV-Ray is found in this order: the path saved with Render ▸ Set POV-Ray Executable…, the environment variable YCRYSTAL_POVRAY, then povray on PATH (command -v povray shows it: /usr/bin/povray from apt, /opt/homebrew/bin/povray from Homebrew on Apple silicon). The include files are looked up in the installation of that executable.

Troubleshooting:

  • Linux: "Could not initialize GLX" or an xcb plugin error: use /usr/bin/python3 outside Conda and install libxcb-cursor0. Without a desktop session run the tests with xvfb-run -a.
  • macOS: python3.12: command not found — install python@3.12 with Homebrew; the system python3 is too old. Conda's Python is unverified.
  • macOS: Qt prints "Can not manage visual effect areas in views without a container layer" for the 3D view; it had no visible effect in the tests.
  • macOS: GUI tests take the keyboard focus while they run; leave the machine alone or run pytest -m "not gui".

Windows 11 (set up 18 November 2026 on a laptop with a 125 % display scale; PowerShell from the repository root). The installation script installs Python 3.12 and POV-Ray for Windows with winget where missing, .venv with the developer tools (-Dev), the Start-menu entry, and checks the renderer:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install-windows.ps1 -Dev
# By hand instead: winget install --id Python.Python.3.12 --exact --scope user;
# winget install --id PersistenceOfVisionRaytracer.POVRay --exact; a new terminal;
# py -3.12 -m venv .venv; .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e ".[dev]" -c constraints.txt
.venv\Scripts\ycrystal.exe --check-renderer
$env:YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION = "1"
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q -rs      # GUI tests open windows for several minutes
.venv\Scripts\pre-commit.exe run --all-files
py -3.12 -m venv .venv-docs; .venv-docs\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
.venv-docs\Scripts\zensical.exe build --clean --strict
  • Windows: the python on PATH of a fresh Windows is a Microsoft Store alias that opens the Store (and hangs a script); use py -3.12 or the venv's python.exe. "The term 'py' is not recognized" means the terminal was opened before Python was installed (VS Code's terminal until VS Code restarts): open a new one.
  • Windows: a clone made from main before .gitattributes existed has CRLF text files (Git for Windows sets core.autocrlf=true), and switching to a branch with .gitattributes does not rewrite them; tests that hash tracked files then fail. Use a fresh clone of a branch that has .gitattributes. (On 18 November 2026 the files of this checkout were converted to LF only where the result hashed to the blob in the index, then git add -u refreshed Git's file information; nothing was staged.)
  • Windows: POV-Ray for Windows must not be open while tests or Ycrystal render (it keeps a single instance; Ycrystal reports it). Run nothing else that renders in parallel with the test suite.

items.title: Decisions and deferred features
items.text:
• FR-VECTOR-02 (CSV/TSV vector tables) is deferred. Its specification is kept in the private plan for possible future use; do not implement or scaffold it unless the user explicitly asks to reactivate it. No feature request has been rejected so far.
  • One repository and one codebase for all systems; no platform branches. Platform checks stay in gui/native.py, desktop.py, render/povray.py, and tests/conftest.py.
  • A resize of the view is not a change of the figure (16 November 2026).
  • macOS CI runs without GUI tests; the GUI is verified on a real Mac.
  • Python: 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 are supported; requires-python >=3.12 (18 November 2026). CI runs 3.12 on every system and 3.13 and 3.14 on Ubuntu only, within the user's limit of twice the 3.12-only CI cost; check this when adding jobs. Windows with 3.13 and 3.14 was verified by hand on the laptop (full suite, 18 November 2026), not in CI.
  • Vectors: Cartesian components in the structure frame; magnetic moments in μB, directions dimensionless; source defaults plus image overrides/suppressions; no inferred signs or magnetic symmetry; styles carry arrow appearance, never vectors.
  • Pictures and custom materials are content-addressed (SHA-256 / content-derived ids); projects embed the custom definitions they use, so they open on a clean profile.
  • Projects/styles are ZIP packages only when they carry a picture; otherwise JSON.
  • Personal materials are stored in QSettings (materials/personal) with thumbnails in a material-thumbnails/ folder (per machine, not in Git; locations above).
  • Preview resolution presets are widths (Small 480, Medium 800, Large 1200, Custom).
  • Gallery (FR-GALLERY-01):
  • The low-symmetry case uses kyanite, COD 1008755 (real, ordered, P-1, CC0, authors credited), not the invented triclinic fixture.
  • The SrTiO3 variants are rendered from the paper figure's snapshot with the cover style, so geometry, camera, and size are identical by construction.
  • Full-size renders stay out of Git. The docs carry only 480 px JPEG thumbnails of real renders, regenerated by the gallery script.
  • The independent-user sheet is the existing checklist, extended; no second sheet.
  • Validation (FR-VALIDATION-01):
  • Images are checked by measured properties, never against stored pixels.
  • Tolerances: sphere centre 0.5 px, disc area 8 %, fitted bounds 1.5 px, scene file 5e-7 Å; each is justified in docs/development/validation.md.
  • Views for image checks are chosen analytically on a 10° grid.
  • The benchmark uses the production command in new processes (median and range; peak memory through a launcher process, see PROGRESS.md).
  • The comparison with other programs rests on their documentation only, quoted with links.
  • Evaluator answers are written only by the evaluators.
  • Snapshots (FR-REPRO-01): the snapshot is an ordinary .ycrystal project (no new recipe format, no project schema change) holding the resolved scene, camera, and output size; the image is rendered from the saved snapshot; image, snapshot, and record are moved into place only after a successful render, the record last. Snapshots drop the absolute path from the structure's import record; provenance paths are relative to the record's folder, files outside it get path: null (name and SHA-256 only). Existing snapshot/record files need --overwrite; the input, style, image, or manifest are never replaced; --render still replaces its PNG. Manifest key save_projects is top-level (schema 1 kept; older Ycrystal refuses the unknown key); report schema 1 gains project/provenance per job. The image SHA-256 is a fingerprint only: POV-Ray writes the render time into every PNG.
  • Batch (FR-BATCH-01): validate the whole manifest first, report every problem, render nothing if any (status 2); sequential jobs; no overwriting without --overwrite; a failed job does not stop the others (status 1); PNG only; paths relative to the manifest; unknown keys refused; max_atoms default 20,000.
  • Views (FR-CAMERA-01): one rule for the window and --view (core/camera.py::axis_view); a, b, c are real-space vectors; a saved camera is kept unless a view, a fixed height, or --camera-policy fit is asked for; fitted views include whole arrows; a fixed visible height that does not fit is an error, never a crop. No reverse views on the command line (--view -a would clash with option parsing).
  • Element mapping (FR-STYLE-MAP-01): explicit only, never inferred; unmapped elements match by symbol; ambiguity (shared targets, a mapped element landing on one with its own settings) is an error, never resolved by order; per-atom settings never follow a mapping; the mapping is not stored in the style. CLI syntax SOURCE=TARGET, - to leave out. The dialog hook is now MainWindow.ask_style_import (was ask_style_parts).
  • Styles from the command line (FR-STYLE-CLI-01): default parts appearance,environment,output (ycrystal.batch.CLI_STYLE_PARTS), display on request; the GUI's Import Style dialog is unchanged. A saved project keeps its camera. A style may not raise the display above 20,000 atoms (LARGE_DISPLAY_ATOMS) from the command line; there is no override. Notes are WARNING: lines on stderr.
  • QE ibrav (FR-QE-IBRAV-01, 21 November 2026): pw.x's lattice vectors exactly (INPUT_PW, latgen.f90), all 20 lattices, pw.x's parameter checks; ibrav = -13 with the axes of QE 6.5 and later (5.2.0–6.4.1 used others); a CELL_PARAMETERS card with ibrav ≠ 0 is refused as pw.x does; crystal_sg stays unsupported. QE's GPL test files are not copied into the repository; scripts/check_qe_ibrav.py downloads them.
  • Element legend (FR-LEGEND-01, 21 November 2026): a 2D layer, never part of the 3D scene or the .pov export; painted onto the rendered PNG at full size after POV-Ray (all image paths), and as an overlay in the live view, by one layout. Sizes are relative: text height in % of the image height, the rest in text heights. Entries come from DisplayGeometry (drawn colours; majority colour per element). Stored in SceneSettings.legend (project schema 8, style schema 3, appearance part). Fitting (window and fitted command-line views) leaves the legend's area free; saved cameras are never moved. Default font: Arial, Helvetica, Liberation Sans, Nimbus Sans, or DejaVu Sans, the first installed. Disabled by default; then images are unchanged.
  • Export (FR-EXPORT-01): one POV-Ray render per export at the export pixel size; pixels and dpi are the source of truth (mm derived); no resampling; JPEG transparency → white; PDF = raster image on a page of the physical size, never called vector; the export does not change the project's output size; dialog settings last for the session only (not QSettings).

items.title: Handoff and maintenance rules
items.text:
• This file is a record of the project's state, not an authorization to implement anything. The order of authority is in CLAUDE.md ("Priority of instructions").
  • At the start of a session read CLAUDE.md, this file, and the requirements that concern the task; then check git status and the recent git log to see the actual state. If a document disagrees with the code or the history, investigate; do not assume the document is right.
  • After a substantial task, update "Latest development session", the status table, and the next steps, from results you observed. Do not report unrun tests as passed or planned work as done.
  • Keep entries short and actionable. Move finished detail to PROGRESS.md instead of growing this file, and keep unresolved issues until they are resolved.
  • No machine-specific absolute paths, personal details, or credentials in this file.

items.title: Ycrystal progress record
items.text: Last updated: 24 November 2026 (v0.5.0 release preparation). The dated sections below preserve their original verification context.

items.title: v0.5.0 release preparation (24 November 2026)
items.text:
• The documentation source branch merged in PR #48 at 3ad60e0.
  • v0.5.0 includes the element legend (PR #45) and expanded Quantum ESPRESSO reader (PR #47). The local macOS audit at c2fa44a passed 933 headless tests with 10 Windows-only skips, pre-commit, strict documentation, and fresh offline installs from source and wheel. The wheel rendered both a project with the legend enabled and a Quantum ESPRESSO ibrav = 1 input.
  • The maintainer reports the Windows desktop and installer work well.
  • See the release checklist and v0.5.0 release record for packaging and release verification.

items.title: Release-status audit (22 November 2026)
items.text:
Audited the published release through GitHub's API and checked every PR referenced in the handoff's feature table against the Git tags using git merge-base --is-ancestor. The repository is public. Release v0.4.0 was published on 18 November 2026 (draft: false, prerelease: false) and includes Ycrystal-0.4.0-windows-x64-setup.exe; its reported SHA-256 matches the checksum already recorded in the release checklist.

Findings and corrections:

  • Thirteen feature/maintenance rows still said "unreleased" even though their merge commits are ancestors of v0.4.0 (34c803d, PR #41). Relabelled them 0.4.0, including the graphical installer merged in PR #40 (2f427ac). Added the Python-support row from PRs #38 and #39, also included in that tag.
  • The legend (PR #45, 6735400) and expanded QE reader (PR #47, c2fa44a) are merged into main but are not ancestors of v0.4.0. Labelled both "Main only (after 0.4.0)" and corrected the stale QE "in review/not merged" statements.
  • Made the table's first-release meaning explicit: later tags include earlier versions' rows. Public availability, merge status, and release inclusion are separate facts. main still reports version 0.4.0, so its version string alone does not establish that a feature is in the tag or downloadable installer.
  • Verified all CI and Windows installer checks at the release tag succeeded (runs 44408274074 and 44408273918); filled the release checklist's previously unspecified tag-CI entry. CI at the QE merge also succeeded on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows.
  • Clarified the release/development distinction on the documentation home page and in the changelog; removed obsolete next steps to commit/merge already merged PRs. Older dated verification records remain historical evidence.

Verification of these source corrections: checked 27 PR references in the table against tag ancestry; strict documentation build reported no issues; pre-commit hooks and git diff --check passed on the changed files. Application code and release artifacts were not changed.

items.title: Documentation publication (22 November 2026)
items.text:
At the user's request, created and pushed gh-pages with only the generated Zensical site and .nojekyll, starting an independent history at 199b419. GitHub Pages reports source gh-pages, path /, build type legacy, HTTPS enforced, and status built. The documentation is publicly available at ymatterlab.github.io/ycrystal.

Prepared source changes on docs/github-pages: canonical site_url, links from the README and home page, publication instructions, and a workflow that strictly builds documentation on main, updates gh-pages without force, and explicitly requests a Pages build. It uses the existing documentation lock and the standard GITHUB_TOKEN; no additional secret is needed. Automatic publishing remains unverified until that source branch is merged and its workflow runs.

Verified:

  • .venv-docs/bin/zensical build --clean --strict: no issues.
  • Checked 36 generated HTML pages and 5,310 local links, anchors, and assets: all targets resolve; sitemap uses the canonical GitHub Pages URL.
  • First GitHub Pages deployment: successful (Actions run).
  • Live HTTP 200 responses for the home, installation, first-figure tutorial, camera reference, documentation workflow, logo, rendered example, search index, and sitemap; home-page styles and scripts also load. Confirmed the deployed Camera.project anchor.
  • Pre-commit hooks passed on the publishing workflow, site configuration, README, documentation home, and publication instructions; workflow YAML and TOML parsed.

items.title: FR-QE-IBRAV-01: Quantum ESPRESSO input with ibrav other than 0 (post-0.4.0, 21 November 2026)
items.text:
Requested by the user on 21 November 2026: support pw.x inputs with ibrav ≠ 0; first check whether ASE supports them, and if not, whether the code in the local utils/ folder (external code, ignored by Git) can read them. Branch feature/qe-ibrav from main at 1aae367. Run on the Linux Mint laptop (Python 3.12.3, ASE 3.29.0).

Subsequently merged in PR #47 (c2fa44a) on 21 November 2026 after CI passed on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows. Available from main, after the v0.4.0 tag.

Findings:

  • ASE 3.29.0 (the pinned version) does not read or write ibrav ≠ 0: read_espresso_in raises "ASE does not support ibrav != 0", and no other part of ASE converts ibrav. ASE 3.22.1 had ibrav_to_cell (its wheel from PyPI was inspected); it was later removed.
  • utils/autoph/pw_utils.py::ibrav_to_cell is ASE 3.22.1's function (identical text) with two changes: a fix of its ibrav = 11 row (a typo that made it fail) and an added ibrav = -13. Checked against QE's Modules/latgen.f90: the lattices it has are right; it has no ibrav = 91 and checks no parameters (a missing c gives a flat cell). It is LGPL code from ASE, inside a repository licensed MIT.

Delivered:

  • io/qe_lattice.py, an own implementation from the pw.x input documentation (INPUT_PW) and latgen.f90: IBRAV_LATTICES (all 20 values pw.x accepts), celldm_from_input (celldm(1…6) or A, B, C, cosAB, cosAC, cosBC with pw.x's abc2celldm mapping), ibrav_cell, and LatticeError with pw.x's checks. For ibrav = -13 the axes of QE 6.5 and later.
  • io/readers.py: QE input with ibrav ≠ 0 opens; alat positions use a; a CELL_PARAMETERS card together with ibrav ≠ 0 is refused (as pw.x does); the source record keeps qe_ibrav and qe_celldm. crystal_sg stays unsupported.
  • Fixtures Si_ibrav2.pw.in, MgB2_ibrav4.pw.in, SrTiO3_ibrav1.pw.in, triclinic_ibrav14.pw.in, and qe_ibrav4_no_c.pw.in (still refused, replacing the removed qe_ibrav2.pw.in in the GUI and command-line rejection tests).
  • scripts/check_qe_ibrav.py: compares with pw.x's output in QE's test suite.
  • Documentation: formats, support matrix, limitations, validation (section F), comparison, architecture, API reference, changelog; CI doctests include the module.
Check Result tests/test_qe_lattice.py (67 tests): the vectors of all 20 lattices as written in INPUT_PW; conventional cell and centring vectors as whole-number combinations, volume ratio, right-handedness; rhombohedral angle and threefold axes; triclinic lengths and angles; the A, B, C, cos… → celldm slots; refused parameters Pass tests/test_readers.py (50 tests): Si, MgB2, SrTiO3, triclinic via ibrav 2, 4, 1, 14 equivalent to their POSCAR/CIF/ibrav = 0 files (within 1e-6 Å); alat positions; 9 refused inputs with messages Pass scripts/check_qe_ibrav.py against QE develop (test-suite/pw_lattice-ibrav): 17 lattices (QE has none for −9, 91, −13) 17 of 17 agree: axes within 4.7e-7 alat (pw.x prints 6 decimals), positions within 1.5e-8 alat Cross-check with the utils function (local only; utils/ is not in the repository): 19 lattices × 200 random parameter sets × both input forms 7,600 cells, largest difference 3.6e-15 Å; ibrav = 91 is not in the utils function Content detection of ibrav inputs named scf.in and input Detected as QE and read Full suite YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -q -rs 1043 passed, 10 skipped (Windows-only tests); after the audit and the Fortran-number and expression fix: 1115 passed, 10 skipped (Windows-only) CI doctest list, scripts/docs_examples.py, pre-commit run --all-files, zensical build --clean --strict Pass

QE versions (asked for by the user, documented in docs/guide/qe-lattices.md): QE's release notes and the source of latgen.f90 at 23 tags (4.3.2 to the development branch) were read and the code of each ibrav compared as text. Only ibrav = -13 changed (QE 6.5: v1(old) = −v2, v2(old) = v1; release notes give (x, y, z) → (y, −x, z) for old crystal positions); -9 appeared in 5.0, 91 and -13 in 5.2.0, -3 in 6.2.0. The A, B, C, cos… mapping is as today from 6.3 (6.2.x ignored cosAC for −13); the bohr changed from CODATA 2006 to 2018 in QE 6.6 (Ycrystal keeps ASE's CODATA 2006 value: relative difference below 5e-9). Compiling the old latgen.f90 versions to compare numbers was not permitted in this session (running downloaded code), so the version comparison is by reading only. This also corrected an earlier statement: the current −13 axes start with QE 6.5, not 6.4.1.

Audit of every ibrav (requested by the user, same day; matrix in docs/guide/qe-lattices.md):

  • Committed tests: all 20 lattices against the documented vectors; all 20 through read_structure in both parameter forms (new: 40 tests); lattice geometry for all 20. Tracing the tests showed every statement of io/qe_lattice.py and of the reader's ibrav branch executed (104 of 104; the 7 unexecuted reader lines are older error paths for missing cards and ibrav = 0).
  • pw.x output: scripts/check_qe_ibrav.py --qe-checkout (new option) over a sparse clone of QE's test-suite (development branch): 289 of 289 applicable inputs agreed (17 lattices; A, B, C form for 1, 2, 4, 6, 14); 112 not applicable (no stored pw.x output, structure read from an earlier run, QEHeat trajectory positions); 6 not read for reasons unrelated to ibrav (Fortran 16.D0 masses in ATOMIC_SPECIES in 5, arithmetic in positions in 1; ASE's parser reads neither).
  • Fixed at the user's request, the same day (io/readers.py): card values that pw.x reads but ASE does not are rewritten before ASE parses the cards. Fortran reals with a D exponent in ATOMIC_SPECIES and CELL_PARAMETERS (fortran_real), and coordinates of ATOMIC_POSITIONS evaluated with the grammar of pw.x's eval_infix (evaluate_qe_expression: numbers with e/E/d/D exponents, + - * / ^, parentheses; ^ and signs bind tightest and group from the right; division by zero and non-real powers refused), read from QE's UtilXlib/eval_infix.c and Modules/read_cards.f90. Plain numbers are left exactly as they were. After the fix: 295 of 295 applicable ibrav ≠ 0 inputs agree (the 6 now read and agree, among them QE's own expression test pw_eval/eval_infix.in); QE's 37 applicable ibrav = 0 inputs agree too (a separate check of the same kind), none unreadable. Tests: 31 new in tests/test_readers.py (grammar, precedence, errors, Fortran reals, files).
  • A grep of QE's whole test suite and example folders found no input with ibrav −9, 91, or −13, so no pw.x reference exists for them in QE.
  • Independent code (the utils copy of ASE 3.22.1's function) and the 17-lattice check were rerun: unchanged.

Not verified: ibrav −9, 91, and −13 against a pw.x run (they rest on the documented vectors, and −9 and −13 on the utils cross-check); inputs written for QE 6.4.1 or older with ibrav = -13 and crystal positions open with the current axes (not detected); running the pw.x comparison script on real macOS and Windows machines; opening such a file in the window by hand. CI has passed on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows.

items.title: FR-LEGEND-01: element legend (post-0.4.0, 21 November 2026)
items.text:
Requested by the user on 21 November 2026, with a reference image (a POV-Ray figure with "● Be ● Sc ● Ru" under the structure): a customizable, publication-quality legend of the displayed elements, drawn independently of the 3D pipeline and exported with the figure. Branch feature/element-legend, from main at 844775d; merged in PR #45 (merge commit 6735400). Run on the Linux Mint laptop (Python 3.12.3, PySide6 6.12.0, VTK 9.7.2, POV-Ray 3.7.0.10).

Delivered:

  • core/legend.py (no Qt): LegendSettings (enabled, layout, position with custom centre, font family and size, text colour, marker size and style, spacing, margin, background with colour and opacity, order with a custom list; validated), stored as SceneSettings.legend; legend_entries reads elements and colours from DisplayGeometry, so the markers have the drawn colours (overrides, own-pigment materials; hidden elements leave the legend).
  • render/legend.py (QtGui, no window): one layout computed at a reference text size and scaled to the image (text height = % of image height, everything else in text heights), glyph outlines without hinting or subpixel antialiasing, shaded or flat markers with a darker outline; draw_legend_on_file paints onto the rendered PNG in place (pixels outside the legend, alpha, and text chunks kept; no resolution chunk added); legend_overlay for the live view; legend_fit_region for fitting. The command line creates a windowless QGuiApplication (offscreen on Linux and macOS, the native plug-in on Windows: gui/native.py::painting_platform).
  • Render jobs: prepare_job(..., legend=); finish_job paints the legend, so the preview, renders, PNG/PDF/JPEG exports, --render, manifests, and snapshot replays all carry it. The .pov scene never contains it (the window and --export-pov say so).
  • Framing: Camera.fitted(region=…), Camera.placed_in, ViewPolicy.resolve(region=…); Fit, Reset View, View along, the panel's Fit View Beside Legend, and fitted command-line views keep the structure out of a legend at an edge. Saved cameras are never moved.
  • Window: Scene ▸ Legend tab (gui/panels/legend_panel.py); every change one undo step (spin boxes merge); a legend-only change does not rebuild the geometry; live overlay in the output frame at device pixels (StructureViewport.set_legend).
  • Files: project schema 8 (scene.legend), style schema 3 (the legend transfers with the appearance part; its custom order follows explicit element mappings); older files open with the legend off. examples/publication/styles/*.ycstyle regenerated by scripts/make_examples.py (schema numbers and a disabled legend block only).
  • Documentation: user guide (Export and rendering ▸ Element legend, controls, appearance), formats, architecture, API reference, changelog; CI doctests include core/legend.py.
Check Result tests/test_legend.py (43 tests, no window): settings validation, order, entry colours (override, pigment, majority, hidden), project and style round trips and transfer, fitting into a region (all four edges, fixed visible height), layout scaling (×10 size gives exactly ×10 box), placement, painting (only the legend's box changes, marker centres within 1/255 of the element colour, transparency kept, no pHYs added, deterministic), jobs (painted when enabled, file untouched when not, failure reported), --export-pov note Pass Command line in a new process without DISPLAY (ycrystal PROJECT --render, stand-in renderer): legend markers in the PNG at the computed places Pass (offscreen plug-in, Linux) Real POV-Ray 3.7 render of SrTiO3 with a legend, fitted: marker colours within 2/255, structure entirely above the legend with a clear gap Pass tests/test_gui_legend.py (10 tests, real window): Legend tab and undo, panel controls, live marker colours and their update after a colour override and a pigmented material, hidden elements, Fit/Reset View/View along beside the legend, render box = live box within one view pixel, JPEG and PDF exports, preview, project reopen Pass Full suite YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -q -rs 963 passed, 10 skipped (Windows-only tests) CI doctest list, scripts/docs_examples.py, pre-commit run --all-files, zensical build --clean --strict Pass Time to paint the legend (on top of the render; random-noise images, the worst case for PNG encoding) 0.3 s at 1200 × 800, 2.9 s at 4252 × 2835

Visual checks (scripted, inspected as images): real renders of SrTiO3 at 700 × 700 with the default legend (sphere markers, Liberation Sans) and with DejaVu Serif in atomic-number order; the window with the Legend tab, the live overlay, and the view fitted above the legend.

CI of PR #45: the first run failed on Windows only, in every test that painted a legend: QImageWriter keeps its output file open until it is destroyed, so the temporary PNG could not be renamed over the image ("being used by another process"). Commit ee6f04a encodes the PNG into a QBuffer and writes the bytes with Python. Run 44911218624 on that commit then passed:

CI job Result Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 (Xvfb, POV-Ray 3.7, full suite) 963 passed, 10 skipped, on each macOS 15 arm64, Python 3.12 (POV-Ray 3.7, no GUI tests) 781 passed, 10 skipped Windows Server 2022, Python 3.12 (POV-Ray for Windows 3.7, no GUI tests) 789 passed, 2 skipped docs, pre-commit, Windows installer build and coexistence check Pass

The legend tests without windows, including the windowless --render in a new process and the real POV-Ray render, therefore ran on macOS (offscreen plug-in) and on Windows (native plug-in).

Not verified: the GUI legend tests on macOS and Windows; HiDPI displays; hands-on use by a person on any system. Known limitations: fonts are looked up on the rendering computer (a missing family is replaced, so a project can look different elsewhere); in a PDF the legend is part of the raster image, not vector text; the legend is not part of .pov exports; no dragging of the legend in the view (custom position by numbers).

items.title: Windows installer (18 November 2026)
items.text:
Requested by the user: a graphical Windows installer (PyInstaller, Inno Setup) in its own branch and PR, recommended for users, with the PowerShell installation kept as the developer installation, and the two coexisting without interfering. Branch feature/windows-installer. Design and rules: Windows installer.

  • packaging/windows/:
  • ycrystal.spec: PyInstaller, one folder with Ycrystal.exe (window) and ycrystal-cli.exe (console), ASE as source files, licence texts collected;
  • ycrystal.iss: Inno Setup, per-user by default, optional all-users;
  • build.ps1, with the build tools pinned in requirements.txt;
  • coexistence-check.ps1.
  • Separate identities:
  • the packaged program: Ycrystal.lnk, AppUserModelID YMatterLab.Ycrystal.App (chosen when sys.frozen is set), file type YMatterLab.Ycrystal.Project;
  • the source installation: Ycrystal (development).lnk, YMatterLab.Ycrystal, Ycrystal.Project, unchanged apart from the shortcut's name.
  • Each side removes only its own parts:
  • --install-desktop renames an older source Ycrystal.lnk, and --uninstall-desktop removes one, only if it starts Python with -m ycrystal.app;
  • the source installation no longer takes the .ycrystal default from an existing file type;
  • the installer removes the default only while it names its own type;
  • the packaged program refuses --install-desktop.
  • windows_shortcut.read_shortcut also reads an application id stored as VT_BSTR, as Inno Setup stores it (found by the coexistence check).
  • POV-Ray: not bundled. The packaged program finds and drives it with the same ycrystal.render.povray code. The installer only looks for it, in the same places, to tell the user.
  • CI: new workflow windows-installer.yml (build, packaged renderer check and render, source installation, coexistence check, installer as an artifact). The POV-Ray for Windows set-up moved into a composite action shared with ci.yml.
  • Docs: README and install guide recommend the installer; developer installation, troubleshooting, notices (the installer bundles Python and the packages), architecture, release procedure, windows-port, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING, changelog.
Check (Windows 11 laptop, Python 3.12.10 for the build) Result packaging\windows\build.ps1 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 Passed in 642 s: folder 552 MB, installer Ycrystal-0.4.0.dev0-windows-x64-setup.exe 129 MB; ASE as 15 top-level .py files; licence folders for Python and 38 distributions. One PyInstaller warning, scipy.special._cdflib not found (a hidden import of the SciPy hook) dist\windows\Ycrystal\ycrystal-cli.exe: --version, --check-renderer, a project render, CIF with --style, VASP and Quantum ESPRESSO export, --install-desktop Version right; PASS … 0.14 px; rendered (4.1 s, 3.2 s); read and exported; the VASP 4 file asks for its elements as from source; --install-desktop refused with exit status 1 Ycrystal.exe opened as a click does (first build) One window, no console and no VTK window; own taskbar button with the icon; automatic preview rendered (3.2 s) .venv\Scripts\ycrystal.exe --install-desktop with the old Ycrystal.lnk of the source installation present Replaced by Ycrystal (development).lnk packaging\windows\coexistence-check.ps1 (real Start menu and registry of the user) First run: 2 failures, the installer's shortcut id read as missing (stored as VT_BSTR; Windows itself read it). After the reader fix: all 27 checks passed Installed per user, then the Start-menu entry and examples\SrTiO3-studio.ycrystal opened as clicks do Both opened …\AppData\Local\Programs\Ycrystal\Ycrystal.exe; Get-StartApps: Ycrystal with YMatterLab.Ycrystal.App and Ycrystal (development) with YMatterLab.Ycrystal Installer started without /SILENT The wizard window "Setup - Ycrystal 0.4.0.dev0" opened; closed at once, not clicked through pytest -m "not gui and not povray"; Windows desktop and installer tests; doctests of the changed modules 649 passed, 3 skipped (POSIX-only); 19 passed; clean

Not verified: - the wizard clicked through by a person; - an installation for all users (administrator); - the installer's page shown when POV-Ray is missing; - the SmartScreen warning on another computer; - the GUI tests and POV-Ray tests of this branch on the laptop. They were left out because the user was working at the computer; Ubuntu CI runs them, and Windows CI the POV-Ray ones.

The installer is not signed.

items.title: Installation without Git (18 November 2026)
items.text:
The user pointed out that Git is not needed: the public repository can be downloaded as a ZIP file and installed from the unpacked folder. The README and the install guide now say "Git is optional" and give the download (…/archive/refs/heads/main.zip, unpacked to ycrystal-main) with curl/unzip and with PowerShell's Invoke-WebRequest and Expand-Archive; updating without Git means unpacking the new ZIP and installing again. No code change: the version comes from ycrystal.__version__, not from Git.

Check Result Windows laptop: the ZIP of feature/windows-install downloaded with Invoke-WebRequest, unpacked with Expand-Archive (no .git folder), then scripts\install-windows.ps1 -NoStartMenu in Windows PowerShell 5.1 .venv created with Python 3.12, Ycrystal installed, renderer check passed, "Ycrystal is ready.", 244 s The README's curl -L … main.zip and unzip commands (Git Bash on the laptop) Download and unpacking work; the folder is ycrystal-main with pyproject.toml and constraints.txt

Not verified: installing from the ZIP on Linux and macOS (the same pip install -e . as from a clone).

items.title: Python 3.13 and 3.14 on Windows (18 November 2026)
items.text:
Requested by the user: test the Windows version of Ycrystal with Python 3.13 and 3.14, on the Windows 11 laptop (x64, 125 % scale, POV-Ray for Windows 3.7.0). No code change. Python 3.13.17 and 3.14.10 (python.org builds) were installed with winget install --id Python.Python.3.13 / 3.14 --exact --scope user, next to 3.12.10; py --list shows all three. For each version, a fresh copy of the checkout of feature/windows-install (at f221cba) in %TEMP%, then:

  1. powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install-windows.ps1 -Python <python.exe> -Dev -NoStartMenu in Windows PowerShell 5.1;
  2. YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q -rs (GUI tests with real windows, POV-Ray tests with POV-Ray for Windows), one version after the other because POV-Ray for Windows renders one copy at a time.
Check Python 3.13.17 Python 3.14.10 Installation script .venv created with 3.13; renderer check PASS: … within 0.14 px; "Ycrystal is ready.", exit status 0; 308 s The same with 3.14; 295 s Packages Every pin of constraints.txt from a wheel, nothing built from source: NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1, VTK 9.7.2, PySide6 6.12.0, Matplotlib 3.11.2, Pillow 13.0.0, ASE 3.29.0 The same versions, from wheels Full suite 906 passed, 3 skipped, 12.2 min 906 passed, 3 skipped, 12.4 min

The 3 skipped tests are the POSIX-only ones (symbolic links, execute bit, POSIX permissions), as on 3.12 (906 passed, 3 skipped on the same laptop). The Start-menu shortcut and file type were exercised by tests/test_windows_desktop.py under each version (temporary folders and registry key); the laptop's real Start-menu entry was left pointing at its 3.12 .venv.

Not verified: the script's py search choosing 3.13 or 3.14 when no 3.12 is installed (3.12 is on the laptop and comes first); hands-on use of the window with 3.13 or 3.14.

items.title: Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 (18 November 2026)
items.text:
Requested by the user after reviewing PR #39: Ycrystal should work at least with Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14; requires-python >=3.12; CI jobs for 3.13 and 3.14 only if CI does not become twice as heavy as with 3.12 alone, otherwise record them by hand. PR #38 (3.13 on macOS) was merged first (e5cf291). Commit f581801 on feature/windows-install (PR #39):

  • pyproject.toml: requires-python = ">=3.12" (was >=3.10). The pins of constraints.txt already needed it: NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1, and contourpy 1.4.0 require Python 3.12 (PyPI metadata), so 3.10 and 3.11 could not install them. PyPI lists wheels for 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14 on Linux x86_64, macOS arm64, and Windows x64 for every compiled pin.
  • Ruff's target follows requires-python: datetime.timezone.utc became datetime.UTC (UP017, the same object) in 7 places; no behaviour change.
  • scripts/install-windows.ps1: uses Python 3.12, 3.13, or 3.14 if py finds one, in this order, before installing 3.12 with winget; refuses Python older than 3.12, also in an existing .venv, with a message instead of a failing pip; warns above 3.14.
  • CI: the full suite (GUI tests under Xvfb, POV-Ray 3.7) on Ubuntu 24.04 also with Python 3.13 and 3.14. All systems on all three versions would triple the job time, so the new jobs run on Ubuntu only.
  • Docs: install guide, support matrix, windows-port, constraints.txt header, CLAUDE.md, changelog.
Check Result Local (Linux laptop, Python 3.12.3): Ruff, pre-commit run --all-files, doctests of the 4 changed modules with doctests, zensical build --clean --strict Clean Local: pytest -m "not gui" on the tests of the changed modules (project, readers, style, POV-Ray writer, export, reproducibility, platform, Windows) 213 passed, 5 skipped (Windows only) CI run 44366127112 on f581801: Ubuntu, Python 3.12.16 / 3.13.18 / 3.14.10, full suite with YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 904 passed, 5 skipped on each version; every pin installed from wheels, unchanged Same run: macOS 15, Python 3.12.10, no GUI tests 732 passed, 5 skipped Same run: Windows Server 2022, Python 3.12.10, no GUI tests; then the installation script with -Python 735 passed, 2 skipped; script: .venv created with Python 3.12, "Ycrystal is ready." CI cost, same run 36.8 job-minutes against 20.3 for the 3.12 jobs alone (1.8×; under the user's 2× limit); wall time 9.6 min (the 3.14 job) against 7.0 min

Not verified: Python 3.13 and 3.14 on Windows (since verified on the laptop, see the section above) and on a real Linux machine, 3.14 on macOS; the script's search through py for 3.13 and 3.14 and its refusal of an old .venv (CI passes -Python; no PowerShell on the Linux laptop).

items.title: Windows installation in one command (18 November 2026)
items.text:
Requested by the user after PR #36 was merged (8051f04): "is there a simpler method for installation?", and to implement it like the other work. Branch feature/windows-install, PR #39. Details and the findings behind it: windows-port.md.

  • scripts/install-windows.ps1: after git clone, one command installs Python 3.12 and POV-Ray for Windows 3.7 with winget where missing (winget has the official installer, same checksum), .venv with the pinned packages, the Start-menu entry, and runs the renderer check. When POV-Ray would ask about its editor, it opens POV-Ray once with instructions. Rerunnable for updates.
  • ycrystal --install-desktop on Windows (desktop.py, new windows_shortcut.py):
  • a Start-menu shortcut to .venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe -I -m ycrystal.app (no console window) with the application id YMatterLab.Ycrystal;
  • an .ico drawn from the SVG;
  • the .ycrystal file type under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes;
  • --uninstall-desktop removes all three.
  • POV-Ray for Windows' question about a missing editor (UseEditors on and no cmedit64.dll, per its source) is now reported by windows_engine_conflict() with the remedy, so --check-renderer, previews, and renders fail at once instead of waiting at a dialog in a minimised window.
  • Windows CI runs the script in Windows PowerShell 5.1 into a new .venv.
  • Install guide (script first; the same steps by hand), README, troubleshooting, support matrix, rendering guide, architecture, reference, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING, changelog.
Check Result The script in Windows PowerShell 5.1 on a copy of the checkout in a folder with a space, without .venv (Python 3.12 and POV-Ray already installed) .venv created, packages installed, POV-Ray found, Start-menu entry installed, PASS: … within 0.14 px, "Ycrystal is ready.", exit status 0; a second run took 29 s The Start-menu shortcut and a .ycrystal file opened as clicks do (os.startfile) Each opened one Ycrystal window run by pythonw.exe, no console window; own taskbar button with the Ycrystal icon; the automatic preview rendered. Get-StartApps: AppID YMatterLab.Ycrystal tests/test_windows_desktop.py (7 tests, 4 of them Windows-only) and the editor-question test; the updated platform and conflict tests Passed on the laptop Full suite on the laptop, YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -q -rs (GUI tests with real windows, POV-Ray for Windows) 906 passed, 3 skipped (the POSIX-only tests), 12.4 min pre-commit run --all-files; zensical build --clean --strict Passed; no issues

Not verified: the winget installs of Python and POV-Ray through the script and its editor prompt (both programs and the editor were already on the laptop); pinning the running window to the taskbar by hand.
