items.title: Windows CI with the real POV-Ray for Windows (18 November 2026)
items.text:
Requested by the user after PR #35 was merged (ae01f43): render with POV-Ray for Windows in GitHub's Windows CI job, which povray.org's browser challenge kept from downloading the installer. Branch ci/windows-povray, PR #36.

  • The official installer, unmodified (SHA-256 2B1331641B6F…5BDC8, checked on the user's download), is the asset of a new release ci-assets (not a Ycrystal release; notes give the licence and the source). The job downloads it with gh release download and its own token, refuses another checksum, installs it with /S.
  • First run: the install worked, but every render waited. scripts/windows_povray_probe.py gained --screenshots (window texts and a desktop screenshot when a render times out; the job uploads them). Its screenshots showed two dialogs: "Could not load internal editor – download it?" (every start without the editor DLL) and, from the second start on, the About box (when ItsAboutTime has passed). POV-Ray's source (pvedit.cpp, pvengine.cpp) confirms both. The job now writes UseEditors=0 and ItsAboutTime=2147483647 into the runner's pvengine.ini before the first start.
  • The laptop never showed the editor question to Ycrystal because the user installed the editor during the session (its DLLs appeared in the installation folder); this also explains the first probe render's 90-second wait.
  • The Windows job is no longer experimental and runs with YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1.
  • Users: the install guide asks to start POV-Ray once and settle the editor question; troubleshooting explains the About box (second start, then every 14 days).
Check Result Windows job, run 44254469298 (57f1afd) Renderer check PASS: POV-Ray 3.7.0.0 … 0.14 px; doctests and documentation examples pass; tests: 727 passed, 2 skipped (POSIX-only), 172 GUI deselected Same run, other jobs Ubuntu (full suite), macOS, docs, pre-commit: pass Probe timeout reporting, on the laptop Reproduced the single-instance error box: window title, button, and message reported; screenshot saved

items.title: Windows port, continued on a Windows computer (18 November 2026)
items.text:
Requested by the user: run Ycrystal natively on Windows, keeping Linux Mint and macOS working, on branch feature/windows. Machine: Windows 11 Enterprise (build 26300) laptop, x64, 125 % display scale, UTF-8 system code page; Python 3.12.10 (python.org, installed with winget for this work); POV-Ray for Windows 3.7.0 installed by the user. Details, sources (POV-Ray's own source code for its command line and single-instance rules), and the answers to the ten questions: docs/development/windows-port.md. The user then tested Ycrystal by hand on the laptop and reports that it works well; Windows is supported from a source checkout (CLAUDE.md targets updated), with Windows CI still running without POV-Ray.

  • Found on the real system, and handled:
  • POV-Ray for Windows makes itself the foreground window even when started minimised: the window holds the foreground (LockSetForegroundWindow) while it runs.
  • It keeps a single instance by default: a second copy shows a modal error box and waits. Ycrystal now checks first and explains (windows_engine_conflict), and its own renders take turns (render/process.py).
  • PySide6's QProcess cannot start it minimised: the window's renders run it through subprocess.Popen with a timer.
  • Its user files (include folder, pvengine.ini) are found through the registry's DocPath.
  • Exit status 0 also after a parse error (no image): already handled by finish_job(); messages come from its log.
  • Bug found and fixed during the work: the first version of the Popen backend kept a "running" marker after a window closed with a render in progress, so every later render waited for ever (12 GUI tests failed). Cancelling now reports at once, and the process itself decides whether one runs; a regression test covers it.
  • Interface: taskbar identity (own button and icon) and an .exe filter for Set POV-Ray Executable…, in gui/native.py.
  • Tests: new contract tests in tests/test_windows_povray.py; tests that simulate a missing POV-Ray also hide an installed POV-Ray for Windows; the exported-scene test uses render_arguments(); a time-stamp flake in test_preview_resolution.py fixed.
  • Documentation: install guide and README (Windows section), support matrix, troubleshooting, rendering guide, architecture, changelog, HANDOFF.
Check Result scripts/windows_povray_probe.py Finds pvengine64.exe outside PATH, version 3.7.0.0, include files present; renders with Ycrystal's command line in 2.3–2.8 s per small scene after the first start Tests without windows, real POV-Ray, before the changes 715 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed (a test ran pvengine64.exe scene.ini without /EXIT; fixed) GUI tests, first run with the changes 160 passed, 12 failed (the Popen backend bug above; fixed) Targeted files after the fixes (test_windows_povray, test_render_queue, test_povray_jobs, test_platform; the six GUI files that had failed) 42 passed, 2 skipped; 68 passed then 1 (time-stamp flake, fixed) Second copy of POV-Ray for Windows while one is open Raw: modal "Commandline processing error", no image. .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ycrystal --check-renderer: FAIL with the explanation in 0.7 s Full suite, YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -q -rs (GUI tests with real windows at 125 % scale; all POV-Ray tests with POV-Ray for Windows) 898 passed, 3 skipped (symbolic links, execute bit, POSIX permissions: by design), none failed; 12 min CI's doctest list, scripts/docs_examples.py, pre-commit run --all-files, zensical build --clean --strict All passed .venv\Scripts\ycrystal.exe --version, --check-renderer, --render of examples\SrTiO3-studio.ycrystal, --export-pov, and the guide's PowerShell command for an exported scene As documented; PASS: POV-Ray 3.7.0.0 … 0.14 px; the exported scene needs Start-Process -Wait (& does not wait for a window program) Scripted run of the main window: capture, 3 previews, 1 final render, foreground watched Draws correctly at scale 1.25; previews 2.6–2.7 s; render saved; the foreground never left Ycrystal Hands-on test by the user on the laptop "It works well" (the items tried were not recorded) Documentation audit after the hands-on test (user's request) Windows commands name the programs .venv\Scripts\ycrystal.exe and python.exe; the py launcher needs a terminal opened after Python's installation (checked: with the PATH a new terminal gets, py -3.12 --version gives Python 3.12.10); new troubleshooting rows; status wording; CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING, pyproject classifiers Not run Linux and macOS in this session (their code paths are unchanged; CI of PR #35 checks them); a %TEMP% outside a legacy code page (this computer's code page is UTF-8)

items.title: Windows port, in progress (17 November 2026)
items.text:
Requested by the user. Decisions by the user: native Ycrystal rendering with POV-Ray for Windows 3.7 (pvengine64.exe), and a pushed branch with a Windows CI job. Branch feature/windows from main at 5b72f92, draft PR #35. Not finished; nothing here establishes that Ycrystal works on Windows. Full record, sources, and the experiments still needed: docs/development/windows-port.md.

  • Code.
  • render/povray.py finds POV-Ray for Windows outside PATH (registry Home, the ProgramFiles folders, POV-Ray\v3.7\bin).
  • It starts it with /EXIT /NR +GAscene.log scene.ini, minimised, and reads its log file.
  • It reads its version from the file's version resource, never starting it.
  • It finds its include folders.
  • render/jobs.py and render/process.py use this. Linux and macOS arguments are unchanged.
  • Tests.
  • Fakes are cross-platform (conftest.python_program; .cmd launchers on Windows), and the execute-bit test is skipped on Windows.
  • tests/test_windows_povray.py (10 tests) checks the Windows contract with a stand-in on any system.
  • .gitattributes keeps LF in Windows checkouts, and make_examples.py writes LF.
  • Tools. scripts/windows_povray_probe.py reports how POV-Ray for Windows behaves.
  • CI. An experimental (continue-on-error) Windows Server 2022 job installs the official installer (SHA-256 checked) silently, runs the probe, the renderer check, and the tests without windows.
Check Result Linux, YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -m "not gui" -q 718 passed, 1 skipped (Windows-only), 172 GUI deselected Windows CI, run 1 Installer download blocked by povray.org's Cloudflare challenge; nothing else ran Windows CI, run 2 (job continues without POV-Ray) Ycrystal installs; doctests and documentation examples pass; tests 621 passed, 98 skipped (95 need POV-Ray, 1 needs POV-Ray for Windows, 2 POSIX-only), none failed

items.title: FR-GALLERY-01: reproducible publication gallery (post-0.3.0, 17 November 2026)
items.text:
Demonstration and documentation work after version 0.3.0 on the Linux Mint 22.1 laptop, on branch feature/gallery from main at 0c18079 (PR #33 merged); submitted as PR #34 after the user's review. No application code changed.

What was added:

  • examples/publication/:
  • README.md: cases, files, regeneration, provenance and licences;
  • gallery.json: the batch manifest, with save_projects;
  • styles/paper.ycstyle and styles/cover.ycstyle;
  • structures/: SrTiO3 and BaZrO3, byte-identical copies of the fixtures, and kyanite.

Two inputs are the existing example projects ../MgB2-gradient.ycrystal (3 × 3 × 1, from the MgB2 fixture) and ../vectors-synthetic-afm.ycrystal. - Styles. scripts/make_examples.py gains publication_styles(), which writes both styles deterministically. - Paper: satin, white background, soft lighting, Okabe–Ito colours for the Sr, Ti, and O sites, 1600 × 1200. - Cover: the same colours, ceramic Sr, chrome Ti, ruby-glass O, in the dark studio (reflective floor, point key light). - Neither changes radii, so the cover keeps a snapshot's geometry. - Kyanite. Al₂SiO₅, P-1, 32 atoms, fully ordered; COD entry 1008755, de Rango et al. (1966). Downloaded and kept verbatim with its SHA-256; COD data are CC0, and the original authors are credited in the README and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. It replaces the invented triclinic cell for the low-symmetry case, because that cell has arbitrary atoms and almost no bonds. Ycrystal reads it with Si–O 1.62–1.64 Å and Al–O 1.81–1.99 Å bonds. - scripts/make_gallery.py: 1. copies the inputs to a temporary folder and runs the manifest with ycrystal --batch; 2. renders the SrTiO3 snapshot with the cover style: environment only, then appearance and environment (same camera and size); 3. deletes the inputs and replays every snapshot with scripts/replay_check.py; 4. writes figure-methods.md/.json from the provenance records and snapshots, and commands.txt; 5. optionally writes thumbnails. - docs/guide/gallery.md: thumbnails, explanation, commands, and the figure-methods table of the recorded run. docs/assets/gallery/*.jpg: seven 480 px JPEG thumbnails (17–26 KB), downscaled from the real 1600 × 1200 renders. - docs/development/manuscript-figures.md: four proposed journal figures with draft captions and stated limitations; which panels exist and which are to do (schematic, screenshot, plots). - Independent evaluation checklist: now uses the supplied paper style and the gallery manifest, and asks evaluators to re-open a snapshot in the window. - Also updated: examples guide, CONTRIBUTING (thumbnail policy), changelog, third-party notices. - tests/test_gallery.py (7 tests; 1 with real POV-Ray), checking: - the manifest plans the five figures, with the mapping and the shared scale, and reports warnings; - the structure inputs and their provenance; - the styles equal what the generator writes; - the cover variants keep positions, radii, camera, and size (colours change only through ruby glass); - the documents and thumbnails match the script; - the whole script runs at 0.1 scale, with 7 of 7 replays the same, equal cameras, and a full table.

Choices made while looking at real renders: - MgB2: one cell down c showed a single B–B bond, so the 3 × 3 × 1 example project is used instead. - Kyanite: the default view instead of down c. - Cover: other candidate materials made gold look pale and translucent, so the materials above were chosen. - A first description of the cover lighting as an "area light" was wrong: the dark studio preset has a point light. It was corrected after the methods table showed it.

Check Result make_gallery.py --out artifacts/gallery --thumbnails docs/assets/gallery (1600 × 1200, POV-Ray 3.7.0.10.unofficial) 7 figures. Batch of five 9.7 s; variants 2.6 s and 9.2 s; 7 of 7 replays identical after the inputs were deleted tests/test_gallery.py with YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 7 passed (the script run 24 s) tests/test_release.py (examples, CLI, one windowed test) Passed

Regression on the laptop: - YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -m "not gui" -q: 709 passed, 172 GUI tests deselected, none skipped (210 s); - scripts/docs_examples.py, pre-commit on all new and changed files, and zensical build --clean --strict: clean; - the verbatim COD file is unchanged after the hooks (SHA-256 checked).

Not run: the GUI tests (no GUI code changed), macOS, replays of the gallery on another machine, and CI. Figure 1 (schematic, screenshot) and the plots of Figure 4 are proposals only.

items.title: FR-VALIDATION-01: scientific validation and benchmarks (post-0.3.0, 17 November 2026)
items.text:
Evidence work after version 0.3.0 on the Linux Mint 22.1 laptop, on branch feature/validation from main at e7ec99f (PR #32 merged); committed as 77008d6 after the user's review, PR #33, merged at 0c18079 after CI passed (pre-commit, docs, Ubuntu full suite 7 min, macOS without windows 7 min). No application code changed: tests, two scripts, and documentation only. Evidence report: docs/development/validation.md, with the observed values and the reasons for each tolerance.

What was added:

  • tests/test_validation.py (55 tests; 26 with real POV-Ray), checking:

  • A. Geometry. The scene file holds exactly the shared geometry:

    • atoms with identity, position, and radius;
    • bonds as whole or half cylinders between atom centres;
    • cell edges between lattice points.

    Also: periodic images are exact lattice translations; lattice views are not mirrored; vectors keep their attachment, direction, and sign in every image. - A. Ray-traced images of SrTiO3, SrTiO3 2 × 2 × 1, MgB2 2 × 2 × 1, triclinic 2 × 1 × 1, and BaZrO3: - every sphere at its projected centre and of its projected size, with a mirrored control; - half-bonds in their atom's colour; - arrow heads where projected; - fitted views never cut off (landscape and portrait).

    Views are chosen analytically so that all atoms are visible. - B. Styles. The grey studio style applied to 8 inputs with 2 sets of parts (one with Ti → Zr) changes no scientific data and writes no file. - E. Effects, each comparison changing one setting: - cast shadows; - the area light's soft shadows vs a point light; - chrome reflecting a red floor, against matte and satin; - glass transmitting a blue background, against satin. - scripts/benchmark_render.py. Cases: - SrTiO3 1³, 4³, 8³, 12³; - a resolution series; - plain, studio, chrome, and glass effects; - MgB2 with --style.

Method: each run is a new ycrystal --render process. Recorded: warm-up and timed runs; median, minimum, and maximum of wall time and printed render time; peak memory from wait4. Also: input, fixture, and style SHA-256, and the system. The first warm-up saves a snapshot per case (--save-project).

Peak memory is read by a small launcher process. The first recorded run measured from the benchmark process itself, and its memory column rose monotonically (84.9 → 87.9 MiB). The cause: on Linux a child's ru_maxrss includes the size of the process that started it (inherited at fork and exec), here the growing benchmark process. The same case alone gave 71 MiB. That run was discarded and the measurement fixed. Verified on Linux: a 300 MB parent no longer shows (11.2 MiB for a trivial command), and a 200 MB grandchild is still seen (199.9 MiB). - scripts/replay_check.py: for each provenance record in a folder: - verifies the recorded SHA-256 of image and snapshot; - renders the snapshot with the production command; - compares pixels (largest and mean difference, fraction beyond the tolerance) and reports both systems.

This gives a ready command for cross-installation checks. - tests/test_validation_scripts.py (4 tests; 1 with real POV-Ray): reports, inputs, snapshots, same/different/modified/no-record outcomes, and usage errors. The stand-in renderer moved into tests/conftest.py::fake_povray (now with a colour setting) and is shared with tests/test_reproducibility.py. - docs/development/comparison.md: VESTA, OVITO 3.17.2, and CView 1.3.1, from their documentation only, with quotations and links. None was installed. A research subagent collected the quotations; three key claims were rechecked against the pages: the OVITO POV-Ray removals, where VESTA's -export_img is listed, and CView's planned items. The CView article's full text was not accessible (its abstract was used). - docs/development/independent-evaluation.md: a checklist for two independent evaluators. No evaluation has taken place. The journal's requirement is quoted from a search summary, because the IUCr pages refused automated access; recheck it before submitting. - tests/fixtures/README.md now says which structures are real compounds (idealised) and which are synthetic (the triclinic cell, the antiferromagnet example), and states the licence.

Runs on the laptop (all with real POV-Ray 3.7.0.10.unofficial):

Check Result tests/test_validation.py, tests/test_validation_scripts.py, tests/test_reproducibility.py with YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 84 passed, none skipped (70 s) Observed margins (--junitxml properties) Sphere centres ≤ 0.19 px (tolerance 0.5); disc areas ≤ 3.5 % (8 %); mirrored control ≥ 51 px; fitted bounds ≤ 0.76 px without arrows (1.5); shadows darken 20.4 % of pixels; penumbra 0.46 vs 0.31; chrome red excess 84–124 vs 0 for matte and satin; glass blue excess 49–78 vs 0 for satin benchmark_render.py --quick --scale 0.5 --repeats 3 9 cases. 15–2,969 atoms: 1.7–2.6 s per command at 400 × 300. Studio +0.5 s; chrome instead of satin in the studio +1.2 s; glass in the studio 65 s (56–75). Peak memory 71–85 MiB. Raw data: docs/development/validation-results/benchmark-linux-2026-11-17.json replay_check.py of that run's 9 snapshots, same laptop 9 of 9 identical pixels (largest difference 0), including glass, chrome, area-light shadows. Raw data: …/replay-check-linux-2026-11-17.json YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -m "not gui" -q 702 passed, 172 GUI tests deselected, none skipped (184 s); the GUI tests still collect ruff check/format --check, pre-commit on the new and changed files, scripts/docs_examples.py, zensical build --clean --strict Clean

items.title: FR-REPRO-01: figure snapshots and provenance records (post-0.3.0, 17 November 2026)
items.text:
Development after version 0.3.0 on the Linux Mint 22.1 laptop, on branch feature/repro-snapshots from main at 5b5791f (PR #31 merged); committed as 86ba228 after the user's review, PR #32, merged at e7ec99f after CI passed (pre-commit, docs, Ubuntu full suite under Xvfb, macOS without windows). The user tested it by hand (17 November 2026) and reports it working. ycrystal FILE … --render OUT.png --save-project FIGURE.ycrystal [--overwrite] and the manifest's top-level "save_projects": true save, next to each image, a self-contained snapshot (an ordinary .ycrystal project) and a provenance record FIGURE.provenance.json. Replay: ycrystal FIGURE.ycrystal --render OUT.png. Guide: docs/guide/reproducibility.md.

Design: new module src/ycrystal/provenance.py (no Qt or VTK) over the existing single-figure functions; no new recipe format, no project schema change (a snapshot is a schema-7 project), no new dependency. snapshot_project returns the project with the camera and size that scene_for chooses (aspect lock reset if the shape changed) and drops the absolute path from the structure's import record. render_snapshot finds POV-Ray, saves the snapshot to a temporary file and reads it back, renders that reloaded project with render_png to a temporary image, hashes the temporary files, writes the record to a temporary file, then renames image, snapshot, and record into place, record last; on any failure the temporary files and any folder it created are removed. provenance_record (schema 1) records Ycrystal and POV-Ray versions, the standard include files the scene needs, SHA-256 and size of input, style, manifest, snapshot, and image, the image size read from the PNG, style parts, element mapping, camera policy and resolved camera, explicit and final sizes, displayed atoms, system (OS, machine, Python, NumPy, ASE), warnings, a replay command, and a reproducibility statement; paths relative to the record's folder, null outside it. check_snapshot_target refuses existing files without --overwrite and never lets a snapshot replace the input, style, image, or manifest. Input and style are hashed when read (SourceFile). app.py: --save-project (needs --render and a .ycrystal name; refused with --batch); --overwrite also accepted with it. manifest.py: save_projects (boolean, top level, manifest schema 1 kept), checked in plan_batch, rendered through render_snapshot; the report gains project and provenance per job (report schema 1, additive); the dry run lists the snapshots.

Check Result Evidence Snapshot of BaZrO3 + grey studio + Ti → Zr, view a, width 500: camera and size as scene_for, structure arrays identical, import path dropped (SHA-256 kept), input unchanged; after save and reload, scene_for without options gives the same camera, settings, positions, radii, colours, materials Pass test_snapshot_fixes_camera_and_size_and_keeps_the_structure Replay writes the same POV-Ray scene (.pov identical except the date line, .ini identical): mapped style with fixed view height, vector project refitted, saved camera with a new width, default fitted view, triclinic down c in portrait Pass test_replaying_a_snapshot_writes_the_same_scene (5) CLI: three files and nothing else (no temporary files); recorded SHA-256 and sizes equal the real bytes of image, snapshot, input, and style; relative paths, null outside; quoted replay command; no absolute path of the test folder, checkout, or home in record or snapshot; record keys and order (schema 1); settings, camera, renderer, structure; input and style unchanged Pass test_save_project_writes_figure_snapshot_and_true_record Existing snapshot/record refused (status 1, files unchanged), accepted with --overwrite; a snapshot onto the input project refused even with --overwrite Pass test_existing_files_and_inputs_are_never_replaced Failed render: nothing left, not even the folders created for the files Pass test_failed_render_leaves_nothing_behind Unwritable folder: error, no image, nothing written Pass test_unwritable_folder_writes_nothing Usage errors (status 2): without --render, with only --export-pov, wrong suffix, with --batch; --overwrite alone still refused Pass test_save_project_usage_errors (5) Missing and damaged snapshots refused on replay, nothing written Pass test_missing_or_damaged_snapshots_are_refused Target checks and record naming Pass test_snapshot_target_checks No window toolkit loaded (subprocess, no DISPLAY) Pass test_headless_snapshot_needs_no_window_toolkit Clean profile: a project with a custom material and vectors, a ZIP style with a background picture; sources deleted, registries cleared, replay in a new process with an empty home: same scene, picture staged from the snapshot package, custom material present, vectors equal Pass test_snapshot_replays_without_style_picture_or_materials[False] Batch with save_projects: dry run lists snapshots; report names project and record per job (subfolder too); every record's job, manifest SHA-256, image and snapshot SHA-256 correct; replay command in the record's folder; snapshots load with mapping and vectors; no temporary files; rerun refused Pass test_batch_saves_a_snapshot_and_record_per_job Batch validation: non-boolean save_projects; a snapshot onto an input (even with --overwrite); an existing record; without save_projects nothing changes Pass test_batch_snapshot_validation Batch: failed renders save no snapshot; report has nulls; no images or folders Pass test_batch_failed_job_saves_no_snapshot Real POV-Ray: BaZrO3 from copies of the CIF and style, sources then deleted; replay with the recorded command in a new process: same pixels (tolerance 1 of 255 per channel); recorded image SHA-256 equals the file; PNG 240 × 180; renderer 3.7 Pass test_replay_after_removing_the_sources_renders_the_same_image Real POV-Ray: picture style, custom material, vectors, clean profile: replay has the same pixels Pass test_snapshot_replays_without_style_picture_or_materials[True] Real POV-Ray: three batch jobs with snapshots, each replayed: same pixels Pass test_batch_snapshots_replay_with_povray

Measured on the laptop (POV-Ray 3.7.0.10.unofficial from apt): every replay had exactly the same pixels as the original (largest difference 0 of 255): the three real POV-Ray tests rerun with tolerance 0 (a negative control with tolerance −1 failed all three, so the setting took effect), a 400 × 300 BaZrO3 figure, and four batch jobs (SrTiO3, BaZrO3, MgB2 down c, vectors) at 240 × 180. The PNG files were never byte-identical: POV-Ray writes a tIME chunk and a "Render Date" comment into every PNG, so the image SHA-256 differs between renders of the same scene. Pixel differences across systems or POV-Ray builds were not measured; macOS was not run for this feature.

Observed, not changed: snapshots, like every project written by save_project, have mode 0600 (owner only), because save_project writes through mkstemp.

Regression runs on the laptop (Linux Mint 22.1, Python 3.12.3, POV-Ray 3.7.0.10 from apt): YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -m "not gui" -q 643 passed, 172 GUI tests deselected, none skipped (137 s; 25 new tests in tests/test_reproducibility.py, 815 in all); tests/test_release.py including its windowed workflow test passed after the CLI change; the CI doctest list (now with provenance.py); scripts/docs_examples.py (now also checks the guide's dry-run line); pre-commit run --all-files and on the new files; zensical build --clean --strict clean. Not run locally: the GUI tests (no GUI code changed; the windows would have taken over the desktop session) and macOS; both ran in the CI of PR #32 (Ubuntu with GUI tests under Xvfb; macOS without windows), which passed.

items.title: FR-BATCH-01: render a series from a manifest (post-0.3.0, 17 November 2026)
items.text:
Development after version 0.3.0, on branch feature/batch-manifest from main at a4ba148 (PR #30 merged); submitted as PR #31. ycrystal --batch MANIFEST.json --output-dir DIR [--dry-run] [--overwrite] [--povray PATH] renders the jobs of a versioned JSON manifest (format: ycrystal-batch, schema 1) to PNGs, sequentially and without a window. Example: examples/batch-series.json (five structures, one style, one element mapping, two views, a project with vectors).

Design: new module src/ycrystal/manifest.py, a thin orchestrator over the single-figure functions (load_input, apply_style_file, ViewPolicy, scene_for, render_png); no second renderer, style parser, or camera code, no queue or parallelism (POV-Ray already uses every core for one image), no new dependency. plan_batch validates everything first: top-level layout and schema, unknown keys (typos are errors), unique safe ids, outputs (relative .png, no .. or absolute paths, unique case-insensitively, existing files refused without --overwrite), inputs (present and readable), styles (each loaded once), style parts, element maps (symbols, then targets via the style transfer), camera policies (including a fixed height that does not fit), sizes, and max_atoms (default 20,000; never truncated). All problems of all jobs are reported together; then nothing is rendered or written (exit status 2). run_batch finds POV-Ray before any job (missing: status 1, nothing written), creates the output folder, renders in manifest order, records a failed job and continues, and writes ycrystal-batch-report.json atomically (job id, input and output as given, status, seconds, size, atoms, warnings, error; Ycrystal and POV-Ray versions). Images are copied into place only after a successful render. Status 0 if all jobs rendered, 1 if any failed. --batch refuses the single-figure options; the batch options need --batch.

Check Result Evidence Example manifest: five jobs in order, outputs (one in a subfolder), 600 × 450, Ti → Zr mapping, per-job views, environment-only style parts, vectors kept; validation writes nothing Pass test_example_manifest_plans_five_jobs_in_order One manifest with 19 jobs and 18 different problems (duplicate and invalid ids, case-insensitive output clash, ../ and absolute outputs, non-PNG, missing and unreadable inputs, missing style, bad style parts, bad symbol, absent target, mapping without style, too small view height, bad width, too many atoms, misspelt key, existing output): every problem reported, nothing written Pass test_every_problem_is_reported_and_nothing_is_written Bad manifest files: not JSON, wrong format, newer schema, no jobs, unknown top-level key Pass test_bad_manifest_files (5) A failed job does not stop the others; order kept; failed job's image not written; report summary, order, relative paths; no .part files Pass test_a_failed_job_does_not_stop_the_others Dry run and missing POV-Ray write nothing Pass test_dry_run_and_missing_povray_write_nothing CLI: dry run output and warnings; invalid manifest status 2 with the problem list; failed jobs status 1 with a report; usage errors for mixed options Pass test_batch_command_line_exit_codes, test_batch_usage_errors (6) No window toolkit loaded (subprocess, no DISPLAY) Pass test_batch_needs_no_window_toolkit Real POV-Ray 3.7: the example series into a folder with a space and ü: five 600 × 450 PNGs, all rendered, renderer recorded, inputs/style/project byte-identical; rerun refused (status 2), --overwrite accepted, no .part files Pass test_example_series_renders_with_povray Example manifest paths are relative and exist Pass test_example_manifest_is_listed_in_the_examples

Visual check (Claude, on the Mac): the five rendered images side by side (SrTiO3 and BaZrO3 along a with chrome Ti/Zr, MgB2 down c, the triclinic cell, the vector example refitted), all in the grey studio. scripts/docs_examples.py (run in CI) runs the example's dry run and checks that every printed line appears in the guide.

Regression runs on the Mac mini (macOS 15.8, Homebrew POV-Ray 3.7.0.10): YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -q -rf 790 passed, none skipped (201 s; 19 new tests in tests/test_batch_manifest.py); doctests of manifest.py, batch.py; pre-commit run --all-files; zensical build --clean --strict clean. Linux not run locally (CI of PR #31).

items.title: FR-CAMERA-01: view and framing policies (post-0.3.0, 17 November 2026)
items.text:
Development after version 0.3.0, on branch feature/camera-policy from main at 445ca84 (PR #29 merged); merged in PR #30 (merge commit a4ba148). Reproducible orientation and framing for figures made without a window: --view default|a|b|c|x|y|z, --camera-policy saved|fit, --fit-margin FRACTION, --view-height ANGSTROM.

Design: one pure helper in core/camera.py serves the window and the command line. axis_view(axis, cell, reverse) is the window's former View-along rule, moved unchanged (the named axis points at the viewer; screen up is the first of c, b, a, or z, y, x, that is not parallel; a, b, c are real-space lattice vectors, not hkl plane normals); MainWindow.view_along now calls it. ViewPolicy(camera, view, margin, visible_height).resolve(saved, points, radii, aspect, cell) returns the saved camera untouched with the saved policy (the default without a view), and otherwise fits the framing bounds of DisplayGeometry.points_and_radii (atoms, cell edges, whole arrows) at the final aspect ratio. A fixed visible height keeps the fitted centre and is refused, with the height needed, if the scene does not fit; it is never cropped. batch.scene_for, export_scene, and render_png take an optional policy (None: exactly the previous behaviour), ready for FR-BATCH-01. The structure is never rotated or moved. No schema change, no new dependency. With --camera-policy fit the CLI leaves out FR-STYLE-CLI-01's note that the saved camera was kept.

Fix found by the new GUI parity test: StructureViewport.set_camera applied position, focal point, and up vector one VTK call at a time, and the camera observer reported each call; switching the view from c to x of the triclinic sample read a half-applied camera whose up vector was parallel to the new direction and raised ValueError in the Qt event loop. The observer is now silent while set_camera applies a camera, which reports the change once at the end, as before.

Check Result Evidence Axis conventions: cubic a/b/c/x/y/z directions and up vectors; reverse; triclinic a, b, c along the real-space vectors; Cartesian views without a cell; lattice views without a cell or with a zero vector refused Pass test_axis_view_conventions; doctests in ycrystal.core.camera No options: saved camera returned unchanged; without one, identical to default_camera; repeated runs identical Pass test_without_options_nothing_changes, all earlier camera, CLI, and example tests unchanged fit refits a saved camera, same orientation Pass test_fit_policy_refits_a_saved_camera_and_keeps_its_orientation No clipping, zero margin: SrTiO3, MgB2, triclinic × 7 views × 800 × 600, 400 × 900, 500 × 500 × repetitions 1 × 1 × 1 and 3 × 2 × 1, every sphere inside the image; coordinates unchanged Pass test_fitted_views_never_clip (126 cases) Whole vector arrows (tips) inside fitted views of the vector example, portrait Pass test_fitted_views_include_whole_vector_arrows Margin scales the frame; fixed visible height keeps the centre; exactly the needed height accepted and unclipped; smaller refused with the needed value Pass test_margin_and_fixed_visible_height Invalid policies (unknown policy or view, margin outside 0–1 or NaN, non-positive height, saved with a view or height) Pass test_invalid_policies_are_refused (7) CLI: --view a/c on MgB2 give −a/−c directions in the exported scene, b up for c; portrait frame; --view-height 30 gives a 30 Å up vector Pass test_views_from_command_line CLI: saved camera kept with no option and with --camera-policy saved; fit after a style changed MgB2's 3 × 3 × 1 to 2 × 2 × 1 keeps the direction, changes the frame, and drops the camera note Pass test_saved_camera_is_kept_unless_asked CLI errors: too small height status 1 with "needs at least 6.14 Å"; conflicts, margin, height, unknown view status 2; options without an output operation status 2; nothing written Pass test_camera_option_errors Real POV-Ray 3.7: MgB2 down c at 160 × 240 (portrait): the image border is background only, atoms drawn Pass test_render_fitted_view_is_not_clipped Window and command line agree: View along a, b, c, x, y, z of the triclinic sample equals ViewPolicy(view=…) (basis, scale, focal point up to depth) Pass test_view_buttons_and_command_line_views_agree

Visual checks (Claude, on the Mac): MgB2 down c (hexagonal cell, b up); SrTiO3 and BaZrO3 down a at --view-height 9, side by side, the larger BaZrO3 cell visibly larger. scripts/docs_examples.py (run in CI) runs the guide's view commands and checks direction, the 9 Å height, and the "needs at least 5.85 Å" message.

Regression runs on the Mac mini (macOS 15.8, Homebrew POV-Ray 3.7.0.10): YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -q -rs 771 passed, none skipped (183 s; 143 new tests: 138 in tests/test_camera.py, 4 in tests/test_release.py, 1 in tests/test_gui_scene.py), twice. One earlier full run reported 1 failure among 771 that did not reproduce in the two following full runs; its name was not captured (unidentified intermittent failure, to watch in CI). Doctests of core/camera.py and batch.py; pre-commit run --all-files; zensical build --clean --strict clean. Linux not run locally (CI of PR #30).

items.title: FR-STYLE-MAP-01: element mapping for styles (post-0.3.0, 17 November 2026)
items.text:
Development after version 0.3.0, on branch feature/style-map from main at f77e163 (PR #28 merged); submitted as PR #29. A style made for one composition can give its element settings to other elements of the target structure: --element-map Sr=Ba,Ti=Zr (O=- leaves O's settings out) with --style, or the rows Element settings go to in the Import Style dialog (gui/style_dialog.py). The mapping is a presentation choice; it is never stored in the style.

Design: io/style.py::resolve_element_map decides, without Qt, where each element setting goes (ElementTransfer); apply_style(…, element_map=None) uses it for element materials, colours, radii (appearance) and bond-pair rules (display, re-sorted alphabetically). Elements that are not mapped keep matching by symbol, so None, {}, and identity mappings give exactly the previous result. Validation, all errors before anything is written: symbols must be chemical elements (ASE's list, case-sensitive, with a hint such as "did you mean Ti?"); targets must be in the structure; two sources may not share a target; a mapped element may not land on an element that keeps its own settings (Ti → O while the style has O settings), and only the parts being applied count. Notes: mapped elements without settings in the style, settings left out with None/-, and structure atoms whose element was mapped elsewhere. Per-atom materials and hidden atoms still transfer only to the same structure; atoms, labels, coordinates, vectors, and bond topology are never changed. CLI parsing (batch.parse_element_map) gives usage errors (status 2) for syntax, symbols, and duplicate sources; structure- dependent errors are ERROR: Element mapping: … (status 1). In the window, MainWindow.ask_style_import replaces ask_style_parts and returns a StyleImportChoice (parts and mapping); rows start at the matching symbol (or Do not transfer), the summary shows what is applied and left out, an ambiguous choice disables Apply, and the import stays one undo step. No schema change, no new dependency. New fixture tests/fixtures/BaZrO3.cif: an illustrative cubic perovskite with a rounded a = 4.19 Å, not reference data.

Check Result Evidence No mapping, {}, and identity mappings give results identical to before (settings and notes), on the same and on another structure Pass test_no_mapping_and_identity_mapping_change_nothing; all earlier style tests unchanged SrTiO3 → BaZrO3 with Sr→Ba, Ti→Zr: materials, colour, radius, and both bond rules (O–Zr, Ba–O) mapped; O by symbol; per-atom material and hidden atom not transferred; coordinates, cell, and element labels unchanged; Zr drawn with Ti's material Pass test_srtio3_style_maps_onto_bazro3 Deliberately partial SrTiO3 → MgB2 (Ti→Mg): Ti settings on Mg; O and Sr settings and both O rules dropped with the usual notes; nothing invented for B Pass test_partial_mapping_onto_mgb2_explains_what_is_dropped Invalid symbols (Xx, ti, mg, a number), absent target, duplicate targets, identity conflict (Ti→O); resolved by O→None or a swap (rules follow their elements); conflicts only for applied parts Pass test_invalid_mappings_are_refused (6), test_mapping_onto_an_element_with_its_own_settings_is_ambiguous Notes for unused mappings and moved elements; resolve_element_map, style_elements Pass test_mapping_notes_unused_and_moved_elements; doctests in ycrystal.io.style, ycrystal.batch --element-map parsing: pairs, spaces, -, identity; empty, missing =, empty entries, duplicates, wrong case, unknown symbols refused Pass test_element_maps_are_parsed (4), test_bad_element_maps_are_refused (8) ZIP style with picture and custom material, original picture deleted and registries cleared: custom material mapped Ti→Zr, picture kept, style file bytes unchanged, saved project keeps the resolved appearance Pass test_mapped_packaged_style_and_saved_project CLI: BaZrO3 + grey studio with Sr=Ba,Ti=Zr: Zr gets the chrome texture, O the ceramic one, a warning for Sr (no settings), inputs byte-identical; ambiguous and absent targets status 1, syntax errors status 2, --element-map without --style status 2, nothing written Pass test_element_map_from_command_line, test_bad_element_maps_write_nothing Real POV-Ray 3.7 render with the mapping: 160 × 120, differs from the unmapped render Pass test_render_with_element_map Dialog: defaults (matching symbol / Do not transfer), live summary, ambiguity disables Apply with the reason, Match Symbols, parts change the check, hidden when the style has no element settings, accessible names; Apply and Cancel buttons Pass test_dialog_defaults_preview_and_ambiguity, test_dialog_without_element_settings_hides_the_mapping, test_dialog_apply_and_cancel_buttons Window: mapped import is one undo step (undo and redo exact), coordinates and labels unchanged; Cancel and an invalid mapping change nothing and add no undo step Pass test_mapped_import_is_one_undo_step, test_cancelled_or_invalid_import_changes_nothing

Visual checks (Claude, on the Mac): dialog screenshots in the default, mapped, and ambiguous states (the summary reserves room so the wrapped text is not squeezed); the guide's BaZrO3 … --element-map Ti=Zr --render shows a chrome Zr in the grey studio, unlike the unmapped render. scripts/docs_examples.py (run in CI) runs the guide's three mapping commands with --export-pov and checks Zr's chrome and the exact quoted warnings; test_documented_walkthrough_with_the_example_style follows the guide's window steps (dialog texts, Apply, one undo step) with the example style.

Regression runs on the Mac mini (macOS 15.8, Homebrew POV-Ray 3.7.0.10): YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -q -rs 627 passed, none skipped (184 s), then the documentation walkthrough test (6 passed in tests/test_gui_style_map.py); 33 new tests: 24 in tests/test_style.py, 3 in tests/test_release.py, 6 in tests/test_gui_style_map.py; pytest -m "not gui" 457 passed; doctests of io/style.py, batch.py, core/scene.py; pre-commit run --all-files; zensical build --clean --strict clean. Linux not run; hands-on use of the dialog by a person not done.

items.title: FR-STYLE-CLI-01: styles from the command line (post-0.3.0, 17 November 2026)
items.text:
Development after version 0.3.0, on branch feature/style-cli from main at 410d87e (0.4.0.dev0); merged in PR #28 (merge commit f77e163). ycrystal FILE --style STYLE.ycstyle [--style-parts LIST] --render OUT.png | --export-pov OUT.pov applies a style without a window. batch.apply_style_file loads the style with load_style and calls the existing apply_style on the input from load_input; the result is a new Project that scene_for, export_scene, and render_png draw as before. No second style parser, scene builder, or renderer; no new dependency; no project or style schema change.

Decisions: the command line's default parts are appearance,environment,output (CLI_STYLE_PARTS); display only on request, because a style's repetitions and hidden atoms belong to its own structure. The GUI's Import Style dialog is unchanged (all four parts offered). The saved camera of a project is kept (a warning when display changes its repetitions); a structure without a camera gets the default view fitted to the styled geometry. A style may not raise the displayed-atom count above 20,000 (LARGE_DISPLAY_ATOMS, now in core/scene.py and shared with the window's confirmation, previously SOFT_LIMIT_ATOMS = 20000 in gui/main_window.py, which remains as an alias) when that is more than the input already shows; the window asks instead, and there is no command-line override. Style notes go to standard error as WARNING: lines; errors keep ERROR: and status 1; usage errors status 2. --render stays PNG-only.

Check Result Evidence Same structure: every requested part, no notes Pass test_same_structure_receives_every_requested_part Different composition (SrTiO3 style → MgB2): default parts leave repetitions, bonds, and hidden atoms; notes for absent elements and per-atom overrides; input project not modified; structure shared, not copied Pass test_cli_default_parts_leave_display_settings_alone; doctest in ycrystal.batch Saved project target (vectors-synthetic-afm.ycrystal): camera and vectors kept, arrow appearance transferred, coordinates unchanged, file bytes unchanged, camera warning when repetitions change Pass test_saved_project_keeps_camera_vectors_and_structure, test_style_on_a_saved_project_keeps_its_camera_and_vectors (identical location/look_at and arrow lines in the exported scene) ZIP style with a background picture and a custom material, original picture deleted and registries cleared: applied, picture staged next to the exported scene, custom declaration written; paths with spaces and non-ASCII Pass test_packaged_style_with_picture_and_custom_material Parts: parsing, order, duplicates; empty, empty entry, unknown, wrong case refused; --style-parts without --style; --style without an output operation is a usage error (no window) Pass test_style_parts_are_parsed, test_bad_style_parts_are_refused, test_style_usage_errors Sizes: style size by default; --width and --height override each on its own; without output the input's size stays Pass test_command_line_sizes_override_the_style (5 cases) Large display (30 × 30 × 30 SrTiO3 with display) refused before writing; without display applied; a project already that large draws as saved Pass test_large_display_from_a_style_is_refused, test_style_errors_write_nothing Missing and damaged style, large display, missing POV-Ray: status 1, ERROR:, output folder stays empty; inputs (style and structure) byte-identical afterwards; without --style the output is as before Pass test_style_errors_write_nothing, test_style_from_command_line No window toolkit: the --style --export-pov path, run without DISPLAY, loads no PySide6, vtk, or pyvista module Pass test_style_command_needs_no_window_toolkit (subprocess) Real POV-Ray 3.7 render with a style: 200 × 150 PNG, differs from the unstyled render, warnings printed, no stray files Pass test_render_with_style_from_command_line

Visual check (Claude, on the Mac): ycrystal tests/fixtures/MgB2.cif --style examples/grey-studio.ycstyle --render MgB2.png (800 × 600 and 400 × 300) shows MgB2 1 × 1 × 1 in the grey studio with floor shadows; with --style-parts appearance,display,environment,output 2 × 2 × 1, refitted; the vector example keeps its camera and arrows.

Regression runs on the Mac mini (macOS 15.8, Homebrew POV-Ray 3.7.0.10): YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -q -rs 595 passed, none skipped (180 s; 29 new tests: 15 in tests/test_style.py, 14 in tests/test_release.py); pytest -m "not gui" 430 passed; doctests of core/scene.py, io/style.py, batch.py and scripts/docs_examples.py (which now runs the guide's MgB2 --style command with --export-pov and checks its exact warning, 800 × 600 size, and studio); pre-commit run --all-files; zensical build --clean --strict clean.
