items.title: FR-EXPORT-01: PDF and JPEG export with publication sizes (post-0.2.0, 16 November 2026)
items.text:
Development after version 0.2.0; merged in PR #23 (merge commit 52b3e5e). Render ▸ Render Image… (Ctrl+R; formerly Render PNG…) opens one dialog: format (PNG default, PDF, JPEG), size (the Render panel's output size, Single column 85 mm at 600 dpi, Double column 180 mm at 600 dpi, Custom), width × height in px or mm, resolution (300/600 offered, 1–100 000 dpi accepted), shape lock, JPEG quality, and destination. POV-Ray renders once at the export pixel size with the unchanged camera, geometry, and environment; only the last step differs per format (render/formats.py). The settings persist for the session.

Check Result Evidence 1. PNG compatibility: render_png(path) copies the POV-Ray file byte for byte (no resolution chunk); from the dialog the PNG gains only a pHYs chunk, with identical compressed image data and pixels; an existing pHYs is replaced; damaged/truncated PNGs are reported Pass test_png_without_resolution_is_copied_byte_for_byte, test_png_resolution_is_added_without_touching_the_pixels, test_an_existing_png_resolution_is_replaced, test_damaged_png_is_reported, test_render_png_keeps_its_former_behaviour; the existing render tests unchanged 2. PDF: valid header and end marker; page size equals the physical size within half a point (Qt writes whole points); the image is embedded once at its rendered pixel size with Flate (no DCT); transparency kept as a soft mask; title stored Pass test_pdf_page_has_the_physical_size_and_the_full_image (2008 × 1339 at 600 dpi; portrait 300 × 450 at 150 dpi), test_pdf_keeps_a_transparent_background 3. JPEG: rendered size, JFIF resolution, colours; quality 10 < 95 < 100 in file size; transparent background white; half-transparent pixels blend to grey Pass test_jpeg_has_the_rendered_size_resolution_and_colours, test_jpeg_quality_changes_the_file, test_jpeg_fills_transparency_with_white, test_jpeg_blends_partly_transparent_edges_with_white 4. Sizes: 85 mm/600 dpi → 2008 px, 180 mm/600 dpi → 4252 px; heights for 3:2, 1:1, 2:3, 16:9 frames within one pixel of the shape; custom combinations including 1200 dpi; px ↔ mm round trip; physical size from pixels and dpi Pass test_publication_presets_give_the_documented_pixel_widths, test_height_follows_the_frame_shape, test_custom_width_and_resolution_combinations, test_units_convert_both_ways_without_drift, test_options_report_the_physical_size; doctests in ycrystal.core.export 5. Validation: sides 16–20 000 px, at most 150 megapixels, 1–100 000 dpi, quality 1–100, PDF needs a resolution and pages ≤ 5080 mm; unknown formats refused; suffixes follow the format (.jpg/.jpeg kept, SrTiO3 v1.2 gets .png appended) Pass test_invalid_settings_are_rejected_with_an_explanation, test_valid_extremes_are_accepted, test_file_suffixes_follow_the_format 6. Files: paths with spaces and non-ASCII characters (Figures für Ångström ✓/new folder/SrTiO₃ figure 1) for each format; a write error leaves no .part file, and an export that fails keeps the previous file Pass test_paths_with_spaces_and_non_ascii_characters, test_write_errors_leave_no_partial_file, test_a_failed_export_keeps_the_previous_file 7. Dialog: PNG at the output size by default; presets set mm and dpi and follow landscape and portrait frames; editing a preset switches to Custom and keeps the values; mm keep the physical size when the dpi changes, px keep the pixels; height edits compute the width; unlocking allows any shape and explains it; invalid entries and an empty file name disable Render; format changes the suffix, shows JPEG quality (and the white-background note only for transparent backgrounds) and the PDF raster note; remembered choices follow a new frame Pass tests/test_gui_export.py (dialog tests) 8. Window: each format written through the same render path with a stand-in renderer; scene revision, output size, camera, environment, and modified state unchanged; status bar names format and size; the action opens the dialog; a write failure shows "Could Not Save Image" and leaves no partial file Pass test_render_image_writes_each_format_without_changing_the_scene, test_render_image_action_uses_the_dialog_answer, test_a_failed_write_is_reported 9. Real POV-Ray 3.7 (Homebrew, macOS): one scene rendered as PNG, PDF, and JPEG at 40 mm, 150 dpi (236 × 157 px) into a non-ASCII folder: equal pixel sizes, PNG and JPEG at 150 dpi, JPEG within mean 4 levels of the PNG, PDF page within half a point of the physical size with the full image; camera, output size, and modified state unchanged Pass test_same_scene_as_png_pdf_and_jpeg Dialog layout on macOS (screenshots of the PNG, JPEG, and unlocked PDF states) Pass (scripted) screenshots in the session's scratch folder (not kept) CI of PR #23: Ubuntu 24.04 full suite under Xvfb with POV-Ray 3.7 (including all new tests); macOS 15 tests without windows; pre-commit; docs Pass GitHub Actions run 43883106317 Hands-on use Pass (user report) The user reported that everything works (16 November 2026) PDF opened in specific viewers (Acrobat, Preview) and journal submission systems Unverified by Claude

Decisions: pixel size and dpi are the source of truth; millimetres are derived (a PDF page is the rendered pixels at the chosen dpi, so 85 mm at 600 dpi becomes 2008 px and an 85.005 mm page). Exports never resample. JPEG composites transparency over white (not the live-view colour of a transparent environment). PDF uses QPdfWriter with LosslessImageRendering; the page box is in whole points (≤ 0.18 mm difference), with the image centred without distortion. Exports do not change the project's output size, so the Render panel and saved projects are unaffected. No new dependency.

Regression runs on the Mac mini (macOS 15.8, Homebrew POV-Ray 3.7.0.10): YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -q -rs 565 passed, none skipped (179 s; 60 new tests: 43 in tests/test_export.py, 17 in tests/test_gui_export.py); after a final one-line dialog change test_export.py, test_gui_export.py, and test_gui_render.py 72 passed and pytest -m "not gui" 400 passed; doctests of the CI list including the two new modules; ruff, pre-commit run --all-files, zensical build --clean --strict clean. Linux: CI of PR #23 (Ubuntu, full suite) passed.

items.title: FR-VECTOR-01: manual atom-attached vectors (post-0.2.0, 15 November 2026)
items.text:
Development after version 0.2.0; merged in PR #19. Edit ▸ Vectors… (and Vectors… in the Appearance tab) attaches Cartesian direction or magnetic-moment (μB) arrows to atoms, as source defaults for all periodic images or as image overrides (including suppression), with centred or tail-at-centre arrows, uniform or proportional length, and independent colour and material. One resolver produces arrow geometry for both renderers. FR-VECTOR-02 (table import/export) is deferred and not started.

Check Result Evidence 1. Endpoints for a known direction (3, 0, 4): centred r ∓ L u/2, tail r → r + L u, head inside the length; proportional L = scale × |v|; reversal swaps tail and tip; arrows along ±x/±y/±z; short-arrow policy (head ≤ 60 % of L, cross-section scaled); zero vector and modulus ≤ 1e-9 draw nothing; non-zero vectors shorter than 1e-4 Å when proportional draw nothing; hidden records; non-finite/wrong-length/unknown-meaning values and invalid sizes rejected; arrows identical for any camera and atom radius Pass test_endpoints_placements_and_length_modes, test_short_arrows_zero_and_invalid_values, test_geometry_does_not_depend_on_camera_or_radii; doctest in ycrystal.core.vectors 2. Source defaults with the same components on every image (opposite moments on two Fe sites, 2 × 1 × 1, no inferred alternation); image override and one-image suppression; boundary images (8 Sr corners); hexagonal (non-orthogonal) cell: midpoints at exact instance positions, components Cartesian; repetition shrink keeps but hides an override, restore shows it; hidden host hides its arrow Pass test_source_defaults_overrides_suppression_and_no_inferred_signs, test_boundary_images_non_orthogonal_cell_hiding_and_repetitions 3. POV cylinders and cones equal the shared geometry (parsed, 1e-6 Å); comments name atom, image, components, unit; live-view mesh bounds equal the arrow extents; real POV-Ray 3.7 renders of synthetic ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and canted examples show the arrows with the body-centre tip at its projected pixel; no arrows without vectors Pass test_writer_arrows_match_the_shared_geometry, test_live_view_matches_shared_geometry_and_leaves_picking_measuring_lighting, test_rendered_ferro_antiferro_and_canted_examples 4. Framing bounds include arrow tips (12 Å arrow below its atom); Fit grows with long arrows only when requested; the orthographic eye lies in front of tips toward the camera and the gradient backdrop behind tips away from it; the floor lies below an arrow pointing down; lighting rig (atom/cell bounds) unchanged by vector changes; picking at every atom unchanged; distance unchanged Pass test_bounds_fit_lighting_and_floor_include_arrows_correctly, test_eye_and_backdrop_stay_clear_of_long_arrows, test_live_view_matches_shared_geometry_and_leaves_picking_measuring_lighting 5. Editor: live preview without undo step or modified flag, frozen targets, Cancel restores, Apply one step (batch), undo/redo; table actions Reverse, Show/Hide, Suppress, Remove (override removal restores the default), row Edit keeps visibility, row selection highlights hosts; appearance edits merge (two length changes → one step), proportional mode; independent arrow colour; custom material only on arrows; a vector change during a running preview discards the stale result; status bar shows the selected atom's vector Pass test_editor_preview_cancel_and_apply_as_one_step, test_table_actions_overrides_suppression_and_opposing_moments, test_appearance_edits_merge_and_custom_arrow_material_persists, test_vector_change_discards_a_running_preview, test_eye_and_backdrop_stay_clear_of_long_arrows 6. Projects (schema 7) round-trip components at full precision, suppressions, hidden records, appearance, and an arrow-only custom material on a clean profile; existing examples load without vectors; an out-of-range attachment is refused; styles carry the appearance only, and importing a style keeps the target's vectors; another structure starts without vectors Pass test_projects_round_trip_and_styles_never_carry_vectors, test_appearance_edits_merge_and_custom_arrow_material_persists, test_style_import_keeps_vectors_and_new_structure_clears_them 7. Example examples/vectors-synthetic-afm.ycrystal (synthetic two-site cell, ±2.2 μB) generated by scripts/make_examples.py and rendered with ycrystal … --render; user guide (Controls ▸ Vectors), reference, architecture Pass command-line render (1.0 s) GUI on the Mint display (scripted, real POV-Ray): Vectors window with source defaults and a canted image override, editor, live view with arrows and the selected host, POV-Ray preview Pass (scripted) artifacts/vectors/vectors-window.png, vector-editor.png, window-vectors.png (gitignored) Hands-on use by a person; very many arrows (live-view mesh speed) Unverified

Decisions: vectors live in SceneSettings (vectors: source defaults and image overrides; vector_style: appearance), so undo, projects, and geometry building reuse the existing paths; one vector per displayed atom; the record identity is its attachment (source index or atom id). DisplayGeometry.arrows holds the resolved geometry; points_and_radii() includes arrows (Fit, eye, backdrop, floor), bounding_sphere() does not (lights). Zero tolerance 1e-9 (modulus), minimum drawn length 1e-4 Å, head at most 60 % of the length. Default appearance: centred, uniform 2.6 Å, satin, dark red. Arrows are drawn as cylinder + cone in POV-Ray and as one non-pickable mesh in VTK. Live view and POV-Ray materials are not claimed to match pixel for pixel.

Regression runs: pytest -m "not povray" 420 passed (strict mode; 14 new non-POV-Ray tests at that point, plus test_eye_and_backdrop_stay_clear_of_long_arrows added and passing afterwards; three existing schema assertions now read 7); pytest -m povray on test_vectors.py, test_background_image.py, test_custom_materials.py, test_gui_material_editor.py, test_gui_render.py, test_gui.py, test_preview_resolution.py, test_povray_jobs.py, and the command-line render 12 passed; test_presets.py environment, combination, and floor renders 20 passed (the 30 per-material renders were not rerun: scenes without arrows and the thumbnail digests are unchanged); doctests; zensical build --clean --strict; ruff.

items.title: FR-BGIMAGE-01: background pictures with portable assets (post-0.2.0, 15 November 2026)
items.text:
Development after version 0.2.0; merged in PR #18. Background type Image shows a user's PNG or JPEG picture behind the structure in the POV-Ray preview and the PNG, framed in the output frame (Fill/Fit, zoom, frame-relative offsets, brightness, Reset Framing). Projects and styles that use a picture become ZIP packages that carry it.

Check Result Evidence Framing arithmetic: Fit/Fill for wide, tall, square, and extreme pictures in 3:2, 1:1, 2:3 frames keep the picture's proportions; Fill covers, Fit fits; zoom and offsets in frame units Pass test_fit_and_fill_keep_the_shape_for_all_orientations; doctest in ycrystal.core.background Reference validation (digest, size, format, mode, finite ranges), Reset Framing, live colour = picture mean Pass test_reference_validation_and_reset Import: PNG/JPEG kept byte-for-byte when POV-Ray reads them as they are; EXIF orientation 6 normalised to an upright PNG (corner colours checked); content identity (same bytes, other name → same id; same name, other bytes → different id); unreadable, truncated, GIF, missing, oversized files refused with messages Pass test_import_keeps_or_normalises_and_identifies_by_content, test_unusable_pictures_are_refused Writer: self-lit image_map … once backdrop in a light group, no_shadow no_reflection, margin colour layer, mean colour for reflections; transparent output, other modes, and no picture leave it out (record kept); floor not removed; bounds unchanged; built-in thumbnails' scene digests unchanged Pass test_writer_backdrop_and_precedence; existing test_presets.py digest tests Staging: the picture is copied next to the scene under a short content name (paths with spaces/non-ASCII); not for transparent output Pass test_scene_files_stage_the_picture Real POV-Ray 3.7 renders with a labelled-quadrant fixture: orientation, Fit margins at 16.7/283.3 px of 300, Fill crop, zoom 0.5 with offsets (centre at the expected pixel), brightness 0.5 (half linear light), PNG alpha shows the margin colour, EXIF JPEG upright, JPEG, portrait picture in 3:2, 1:1, 2:3 outputs undistorted, square picture filling a portrait output, same composition at 150 × 100 and 600 × 400 Pass test_rendered_framing_orientation_and_alpha, test_rendered_sources_outputs_and_resolutions Glass shows the picture through the atom; an exported folder renders after being moved Pass test_glass_shows_the_picture_and_project_renders_after_relocation Projects: ZIP package (project.json + assets/<sha256>.png), schema 6, reopened after deleting the source and clearing the session registry; projects without pictures stay JSON; existing example projects load; missing picture, tampered picture, unsafe entry name, corrupt archive, and a JSON project naming a picture fail with messages Pass test_project_package_round_trip_without_the_source, test_damaged_and_unsafe_packages_fail_clearly Styles: Environment style with picture as package (style schema 2), reopened after deleting the source; plain styles stay JSON; a schema-1 style loads; corrupt package refused Pass test_environment_style_carries_its_picture GUI: Choose Image is one undo step (undo/redo), marks the project modified and the preview out of date, changes neither camera, output size, nor bounds; live view shows the mean colour; continuous zoom edits merge into one step; offsets, brightness, Fit; Replace keeps framing; Reset Framing; Remove; undo still finds a replaced picture; unusable file keeps the background Pass test_choose_image_is_one_undoable_step_that_changes_nothing_else, test_framing_controls_merge_reset_remove_and_replace, test_unusable_file_keeps_the_current_background GUI: floor notice with Turn Off Floor, transparency notice (picture kept), presets remember the picture; a framing change during a running preview discards the stale result Pass test_floor_and_transparency_notices_and_presets, test_framing_change_discards_a_running_preview GUI: save project and Environment style as packages, export copies the picture; reopen in a new window and import the style after deleting the source and clearing the registry Pass test_project_style_and_export_carry_the_picture GUI on the Mint display (scripted, real POV-Ray): Background group with picture controls and floor notice; preview with a landscape picture Pass (scripted) artifacts/appearance/background-group.png, window-image-background.png (gitignored) Hands-on use by a person; very large photographs (time and memory) Unverified

Decisions: the picture is identified by the SHA-256 of its stored bytes and kept in a session registry, so undo/redo never loses it; it is stored unchanged when POV-Ray reads it as it is, otherwise as an upright PNG. Projects and styles are ZIP packages only when they carry a picture (detected by content, suffix unchanged); limits: 64 MB per picture, 12000 px per side, 50 megapixels; packages up to 256 entries and 1 GB unpacked, with relative safe names only. Preview requests are identified by the scene revision, which every picture or framing change increases. The picture lies on a self-lit plane behind the scene (not in a sky sphere), is excluded from reflections (no_reflection; reflective atoms see the picture's mean colour as POV-Ray background), and is seen through refraction. Applying an environment preset keeps the picture record (not drawn) so that switching back to Image restores it.

Regression runs (both features together): pytest -m "not povray" 406 passed (strict mode; 34 new non-POV-Ray tests for both features, and three existing assertions updated: schema number 6 in test_project.py and test_aspect.py, the reserved custom category in test_presets.py); pytest -m povray on test_background_image.py, test_custom_materials.py, test_gui_material_editor.py, test_gui_render.py, test_gui.py, test_preview_resolution.py, test_povray_jobs.py, and the command-line render 11 passed; test_presets.py environment, combination, and floor renders 20 passed (the 30 per-material renders were not rerun: built-in declarations and thumbnail scene digests are unchanged); ycrystal pkg.ycrystal --render on a package with a picture and a variant (path with a space and ü) rendered with both; doctests; zensical build --clean --strict; ruff.

items.title: FR-MATERIAL-01: custom material variants (post-0.2.0, 15 November 2026)
items.text:
Development after version 0.2.0; merged in PR #18. Customize Material… (Appearance tab, Edit menu) starts from a Ycrystal recipe, edits typed parameters, and applies the variant to the default material, an element, or the selected atoms, or saves it as a personal material.

Check Result Evidence Untouched variants of all 13 editable bases (Matte, Satin, Glossy, Ceramic, Plastic, Glass, Frosted glass, Gem, Marble, Jade, Granite, Stone, Wood) write declarations token-for-token equal to the built-ins; kind, colour behaviour, includes, texture space unchanged; built-ins unchanged Pass test_untouched_variants_equal_the_built_in_recipes; doctest in ycrystal.presets.custom Each control changes its POV-Ray property: diffuse, specular/roughness, reflection, phong/phong size, filter, interior ior, normal bumps strength/scale, gem fresnel reflection, pattern scale of pigment (marble) and texture (stone) kinds; live look follows Pass test_each_control_changes_its_pov_property Invalid values (out of range, NaN, ∞), unknown parameters, empty names, native bases (explanation names T_Gold_3C), unknown bases, newer versions, tampered ids, missing parameters rejected Pass test_invalid_definitions_are_rejected Ids derived from content (custom_<base>_<digest>): same definition → same id, other name → other id, never a built-in id; registration idempotent; editing previews registered unlisted Pass test_ids_are_content_derived_and_never_collide Precedence atom > element > default with periodic-image-specific overrides; bond halves take their atom's variant; readable name/description comments; standard include still external Pass test_precedence_periodic_images_and_bond_halves Projects and styles embed every used definition and reopen on a clean profile (registry cleared) with identical scenes and declarations; style transfer keeps part and compatibility rules; tampered or missing definitions fail with messages Pass test_projects_and_styles_reopen_on_a_clean_profile Real POV-Ray renders: untouched Satin, Frosted glass, Marble variants pixel-identical to the built-ins; specular, ior, bump strength, and pattern-scale changes change the image Pass test_rendered_variants GUI: debounced preview without undo step or modified flag; Cancel restores; Apply is one undo step with undo/redo; menu shows the variant (✎); selection captured at opening; element target; precedence Pass test_preview_then_cancel_leaves_no_trace, test_apply_is_one_undoable_step, test_selection_is_captured_and_precedence_holds GUI: native materials read-only with explanation; glass filter explanation; Reset to Base; pattern-only controls Pass test_native_materials_are_read_only_and_reset_restores_the_base Personal materials: Save as My Material stores the definition in QSettings, gallery lists it (badge fallback icon), it returns after a restart, and a project opens on a clean profile without it; editing during a running preview discards the stale result; a real POV-Ray thumbnail is rendered for a saved variant Pass test_personal_materials_persist_and_files_need_no_profile, test_editing_discards_a_stale_preview, test_saved_material_gets_a_real_thumbnail GUI on the Mint display (scripted, real POV-Ray): Customize Material dialog (Frosted glass), preview with the applied variant over a background picture Pass (scripted) artifacts/appearance/customize-material.png, preview-custom-material.png (gitignored) Hands-on use by a person (dialog flow, gallery browsing) Unverified

Decisions: parameter defaults are explicit data in ycrystal.presets.custom.SCHEMAS (equal to the built-in recipes, checked by tests), and recipe text is generated from them; no POV-Ray text is parsed. Every parameter (including hidden ones such as ambient) is stored, so a saved figure does not change if a built-in default changes. Personal materials are a JSON list in QSettings (materials/personal), thumbnails in material-thumbnails/ next to the settings file. Projects (schema 6, top-level materials) and styles (schema 2) embed the definitions they use; package and asset machinery is shared with FR-BGIMAGE-01 (variants need no binary assets). Native materials and ASE styles stay read-only.

Regression runs: see FR-BGIMAGE-01 above (one run for both features).

items.title: FR-MEASURE-01: distance and bond-angle measurements (post-0.2.0, 15 November 2026)
items.text:
Development after version 0.2.0; merged in PR #16. Distance and Bond angle modes (View along toolbar and Edit menu, mutually exclusive) measure between clicked displayed atoms; results go to a new Measurements dock at the bottom of the window. Session-only: nothing is saved in projects.

Check Result Evidence Known values: 3 Å distance, 0°, 60°, 90°, 120°, 180°; SrTiO₃ Ti–O = a/2, O–Ti–O = 90° and 180°, Sr–Sr images a and a√3 Pass test_known_distances_and_angles, test_displayed_instances_match_the_geometry_in_supercells; doctest in ycrystal.core.measure B is the vertex: the same three atoms in different orders give the expected different angles Pass test_b_is_the_vertex, test_angle_order_vertex_and_repeated_measurements Roundoff: atan2(\|u × v\|, u · v); collinear arms give exactly 0°/180°, large coordinates and tiny angles stay accurate; results always within 0–180° Pass test_roundoff_near_zero_and_straight_angles Degenerate selections: zero-length arms rejected (in the session at the pick that causes them, keeping earlier picks); the same instance twice rejected; wrong counts, unknown kinds, nonexistent atoms, images without a cell rejected; two distinct atoms at one place give a valid 0 Å distance Pass test_degenerate_selections_are_rejected, test_session_rejects_zero_length_arms, test_escape_mode_switch_and_rejected_picks Periodic images: exact instances, no minimum image (8 Å vs 2 Å example); images of one source atom measurable; displayed positions in 1 × 1 × 1, 2 × 3 × 1, and 2 × 2 × 2 (boundary images off) equal positions[source] + image @ cell bit for bit Pass test_exact_images_not_minimum_image, test_displayed_instances_match_the_geometry_in_supercells Non-orthogonal cells: hexagonal (120° and 60° between image directions, |a − b| = a√3); triclinic distances equal the fractional metric-tensor result for 306 ordered instance pairs (3 atoms × 6 images) Pass test_non_orthogonal_cells Independence: camera orbit and zoom, atom size, material, and repetitions leave values bit-identical; values equal those from input coordinates Pass test_results_ignore_display_settings, test_results_ignore_camera_and_appearance Interaction with real mouse events: prompts (“Bond angle: select atom B — angle vertex …”), A/B/C picks, empty-space clicks keep picks, a drag starting on an atom orbits and picks nothing, ordinary selection untouched in the modes and working after them; Esc cancels (a second Esc clears the selection); mode switch cancels; the mode stays on after a measurement; results are appended Pass test_modes_are_discoverable_and_exclusive, test_distance_by_clicks_reveals_the_panel, test_angle_order_vertex_and_repeated_measurements, test_escape_mode_switch_and_rejected_picks, test_drags_navigate_and_ordinary_selection_is_preserved Panel: revealed on the first measurement under the 3D view only (right docks keep the corner); window size unchanged; rows with type, identities with image offsets, results with units and vertex; Copy Selected and Ctrl+C give self-contained lines; Remove Selected; Clear All; full-precision tooltip Pass test_distance_by_clicks_reveals_the_panel, test_copy_remove_and_clear Invalidation: boundary images off removes only the measurement whose ball disappeared and cancels the incomplete one, with a note; undo does not resurrect it; hiding a measured atom removes its measurement; loading another structure clears everything Pass test_session_invalidation, test_invalidation_on_display_and_structure_changes Helpers: non-pickable VTK actors (cages and labels in the scene renderer, dashed lines in a non-interactive overlay layer with the same camera); picking at all atoms and next to the marks is identical with and without helpers; exported scene text, bounds, lights, output camera, Fit, undo stack, modified flag unchanged; projects contain no measurements Pass test_helpers_stay_out_of_exports_bounds_fit_and_picking, test_distance_by_clicks_reveals_the_panel; existing POV-Ray GUI render test GUI on the Mint display (scripted): angle with cages, labels, dashed arms and arc; distance between two Sr images with the dashed line over the atoms; panel with two rows under the view Pass (scripted) artifacts/measure/angle-pending.png, angle-complete.png, distance-images.png, panel.png (gitignored) Hands-on use by a person (clicking in different orientations, keyboard use of the table) Unverified

Design: ycrystal.core.measure (pure) computes positions from AtomIds and the structure, distances, angles, text, and holds the MeasurementSession (mode, picks, results). The window routes atom clicks to the session while a mode is on, shows the instruction in the status bar, passes rows to MeasurementPanel, and passes picked positions to StructureViewport.set_measurement. After every geometry change the session drops measurements whose atoms are no longer displayed (or everything for a new structure object).

Regression runs (on exactly the committed files): pytest -m "not povray" 367 passed (strict mode; 21 new tests, 12 pure and 9 GUI); pytest -m povray on test_gui_render.py and test_gui.py 4 passed (including the POV-Ray render compared with the output frame); doctests in ycrystal.core.measure; zensical build --clean --strict; ruff. Not run: the other POV-Ray tests (exported scenes are unchanged: the helpers are not part of the geometry).

Remaining limitations: revealing the panel shrinks the 3D view like any window resize, so the output camera stays the same but the preview is marked out of date (and refreshed if automatic) — resolved on 16 November 2026: a resize is no longer a change of the figure (see the macOS maintenance section); removed measurements are not restored by undo; the dashed lines are drawn in front of all atoms, so a guide may cross atoms that lie in front of it; a ball hidden behind others must be brought into view (orbit) before it can be clicked.

items.title: FR-PREVIEW-01: preview resolution (post-0.2.0, 15 November 2026)
items.text:
Development after version 0.2.0 (not part of 0.1.0 or 0.2.0); merged in PR #17. The POV-Ray preview dock gets a Resolution selector: Small 480 px wide (the default), Medium 800 px, Large 1200 px, or a custom width (16–4000 px). The height follows the output's aspect ratio. The main viewport stays the interactive VTK view.

Starting point (verified in MainWindow.preview_settings): 480 px on the longer side, never larger than the output, antialiasing off, so 480 × 320 at 3:2 and 320 × 480 at 2:3. The new presets are widths, as requested: landscape and square outputs keep their previous default size, while a portrait output's default Small preview is now 480 px wide (480 × 720 at 2:3 instead of 320 × 480).

Check Result Evidence Presets and rounding: 3:2 gives 480 × 320, 800 × 533, 1200 × 800; 2:3, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1 outputs; never larger than the output; every combination of 36 output sizes × 6 widths is within half a pixel of the output shape and inside the limits Pass test_presets_at_three_to_two, test_portrait_and_other_shapes, test_every_size_matches_the_output_shape; doctest in ycrystal.core.aspect Limits: custom width 16–4000 px (spin box range; other values raise and change nothing); preview height at most 4000 px; each side at least 16 px for extreme shapes (8000 × 16 output → 8000 × 16 preview); the shape is never distorted; unreadable stored values fall back to the default Pass test_limits_keep_the_shape, test_custom_width_and_limits, test_preference_is_restored Selector shows the actual preview size and the final PNG size, with the reason for any limit; Custom enables the width field and remembers its width; portrait and non-3:2 outputs update the shown size Pass test_selector_presets_show_the_actual_size, test_custom_width_and_limits, test_portrait_and_non_three_to_two_outputs No effect on the figure: output size, output settings (incl. lock ratio), camera, exported scene text, undo history, and modified state are unchanged by resolution changes Pass test_selector_presets_show_the_actual_size, test_preview_png_has_the_requested_size POV-Ray receives the requested size (job .ini has Width=800, Height=533, Antialias=off); real POV-Ray PNGs are 800 × 533 (Medium, 1200 × 800 output) and 480 × 720 (Small, 800 × 1200 output) Pass test_requested_size_reaches_povray, test_preview_png_has_the_requested_size (POV-Ray 3.7) Preference persists in QSettings (render/preview_resolution, render/preview_custom_width), not in projects Pass test_preference_is_restored Lifecycle: automatic preview off marks the shown preview out of date and starts nothing; on, a debounced preview at the new size follows; the scene revision does not change Pass test_resolution_change_marks_outdated_or_updates Stale results: the request identity is (scene revision, width, height); a result for an older resolution is discarded with an explanation; a newer request supersedes a running one and only the latest is shown Pass test_stale_resolution_results_never_replace_the_latest; existing test_stale_preview_is_discarded, test_newer_preview_supersedes_older_one Display: the image fits the dock without distortion; resizing never starts a render; a large image or long status text does not widen the dock or the window Pass test_resizing_the_panel_fits_without_rendering GUI on the Mint display (scripted, real POV-Ray): dock at 334 × 272 px with Small, Medium, a portrait Large preview limited to the output, and a Custom width marked out of date; the dock width stays constant Pass (scripted) artifacts/preview/dock-*.png (gitignored) Hands-on use by a person (choosing presets and typing a custom width) Unverified

Design: ycrystal.core.aspect.preview_size (pure) computes the preview size from the output size and the requested width; MainWindow.preview_settings uses it, so preview jobs keep the output's background and the preview's antialiasing setting. The choice is window state backed by QSettings and is neither undoable nor saved in projects. The preview queue tags each job with a PreviewRequest (revision, width, height); the dock shows a result only if its request equals the current one. The dock's status and size labels wrap within the dock width instead of widening it.

Regression runs (on top of the merged FR-MEASURE-01): pytest -m "not povray" 379 passed (strict mode; 12 new tests); pytest -m povray on test_gui_render.py, test_preview_resolution.py, test_gui.py, and test_release.py::test_render_from_command_line 6 passed (other POV-Ray tests not rerun: exported scenes and final renders are unchanged); doctests in ycrystal.core.aspect; zensical build --clean --strict; pre-commit on the changed files.

Remaining limitations: rounding the height to whole pixels changes the preview's frame by less than half a preview pixel (as before); a requested size larger than the output is reduced to the output size, so Large on a small output shows the output size; the shown image is scaled to the dock, so a preview larger than the dock is displayed reduced.

items.title: FR-LIGHT-01: Lighting Setup window and live lighting (post-0.1.0, 15 November 2026)
items.text:
New development after the 0.1.0 baseline (not part of M0–M6), released in 0.2.0; branch feature/lighting-editor, submitted as a pull request. Three increments: (A) one shared helper resolves the lights, (B) a Lighting Setup window shows them in 3D with draggable key-light handles, (C) the live view uses the resolved key and fill lights instead of VTK's default light kit.

Check Result Evidence A: extraction preserves the export: 672 scenes (4 geometries × 4 cameras incl. orbit/roll, pan, zoom × all 6 lighting and 12 environment presets plus custom, zero-intensity, and shadowless area cases × 2 output sizes) byte-identical before/after, apart from the time stamp Pass scripted comparison (scratch script, not kept in the repository); test_reference_example_is_unchanged (the SrTiO₃ numbers of the lighting analysis: key (−20.576, 13.544, 12.458), fill (17.361, −3.551, 23.965), area axes 2.178 Å); test_writer_lights_are_the_resolved_rig (19 presets/cases) A: conventions: azimuth 0 toward the viewer, +90 screen right, elevation toward screen up; orbit and roll move world positions but not view-relative ones; pan adds |C − F| to the distance; zoom and output size change nothing; supercells, boundary images, cell edges, and hidden atoms change C and R as documented Pass test_angles_follow_the_output_camera, test_pan_zoom_and_output_size, test_displayed_geometry_sets_the_scale A: intensities (0 omits a light), area diameter = light size × R with axes along screen right/up, panel at C + 3R × key direction with radius 1.6R, fill always shadowless; inverse angles with wrapping, clamping, and the pole Pass test_intensities_size_and_panel, test_angles_round_trip_wrap_clamp_and_pole, test_guide_arcs_lie_on_the_placement_sphere; doctest in ycrystal.core.lighting C: live view has exactly the two rig lights (scene lights, positional, cone ≥ 90°, attenuation (1, 0, 0), no automatic headlight) at the resolved positions and intensities; they follow orbit/roll/pan, repetitions, intensity changes (0 switches off), and presets Pass test_main_view_uses_the_resolved_rig_instead_of_the_light_kit, test_main_view_lights_follow_camera_geometry_and_settings B: button Lighting Setup… and View ▸ Lighting Setup…; overview shows key/fill (sphere/cube, labels, intensities), F (cross), C (octahedron), output camera (cone and axis) and frame, horizon ring and azimuth/elevation arcs, area-light diameter (wire sphere) and reflection panel when enabled; read-out of D, R, |C − F| Pass test_lighting_setup_opens_and_shows_the_rig; screenshots artifacts/lighting/setup-dramatic.png, setup-studio-like.png B: independent overview camera: orbiting it changes neither the output camera, the environment, the scene revision, the exported lights, nor the main view's props; the overview follows output-camera changes (throttled) without moving its own camera; output-size changes redraw the frame Pass test_overview_navigation_changes_nothing_else, test_overview_follows_the_output_camera_but_keeps_its_own B: helper graphics are excluded from exports, geometry bounds, Fit, and picking (separate renderer and window) Pass test_helper_graphics_stay_out_of_exports_bounds_and_picking B: numeric edits (panel and the window's own keyboard spin boxes, merged like the panel) and presets update the overview Pass test_numeric_edits_and_presets_update_the_overview B: drag with real mouse events: live lights, both spin boxes, and the overview follow without an undo step, revision, or preview; release = one undo step, one revision, the debounced automatic preview starts; undo restores Pass test_key_drag_previews_then_commits_one_step B: Esc in the overview, Esc in the main window (Select None), and the right button cancel and restore lights, spin boxes, and overview; no undo step Pass test_cancelled_drag_restores_everything (3 cases) B: limits and basis: dragging above the structure stops at 89°; the azimuth handle changes only the azimuth; angles are interpreted in the output camera's basis also after orbiting the overview; an unchanged drag adds no step Pass test_drag_respects_limits_and_the_output_basis, test_unchanged_drag_adds_no_step Projects and presets: no new stored state (the project's lighting keys are unchanged); a dragged direction survives save/reopen; presets unchanged Pass test_projects_and_presets_keep_their_lighting; existing project and preset tests GUI on the Mint display (scripted): overview, labels, drag preview and commit, live view lit from the left (dramatic) and from the right (azimuth +60°) Pass (scripted) artifacts/lighting/main-key-left.png, main-key-right.png, setup-after-drag.png, setup-area-panel.png Hands-on use by a person (mouse drags in the overview, Esc, keyboard spin boxes) Unverified

Design: ycrystal.core.lighting (pure) returns a frozen LightingRig with world positions, directions, intensities, shadow flags, area axes, and the panel; it is derived on demand from the environment, the output camera, and the displayed geometry, and nothing new is saved. scene_to_pov writes its lights from the rig. The live viewport re-resolves the rig before every redraw (bounds cached per scene) and sets two VTK scene lights at those world positions, so no second camera-relative transformation is applied. The Lighting Setup window (ycrystal.gui.lighting_setup) wraps a second VTK view (ycrystal.viewport.lighting_view) with its own camera and default readability lights. Drags report whole-degree angles; the window previews them (live lights, spin boxes, overview) without touching the environment and applies the final angles on release through the existing undoable environment command.

Regression runs: pytest -m "not povray" 346 passed (strict mode; 40 new tests); pytest -m povray on test_gui_render.py, test_gui.py, test_gui_appearance.py, test_release.py::test_render_from_command_line, and test_presets.py::test_mixed_overrides_render_and_floor_shadows 7 passed (the other 53 POV-Ray tests were not rerun because every exported scene is byte-identical); doctests; zensical build --clean --strict; pre-commit on the changed files.

Remaining limitations: the live view has no shadows, area-light softness, reflections, refraction, or reflection panel, and its Phong shading is not expected to match POV-Ray pixel for pixel; the overview's labels can overlap when lights, F, and the camera line up in the chosen view (orbit the overview or press Reset Overview).

items.title: FR-RENDER-01: lock aspect ratio of the output size (post-0.1.0, 15 November 2026)
items.text:
New development after the 0.1.0 baseline (not part of M0–M6); branch feature/render-aspect-lock, merged in PR #14. A padlock button beside Width and Height in the Render panel keeps the output shape while the resolution changes.

Check Result Evidence Interface: checkable button, closed/open padlock (shape differs, not only colour), tooltips, Tab + Space, accessible name, locked by default Pass test_lock_button_defaults_and_states; screenshots artifacts/aspect/panel-locked.png, panel-unlocked.png Locked, both directions: 2400 × 1600 → Height 1920 → 2880 × 1920 → Width 3000 → 3000 × 2000 Pass test_locked_editing_links_both_dimensions, test_examples_from_the_request Unlocked: independent edits (→ 2400 × 1920); relocking captures the current ratio without changing the size Pass test_unlocked_editing_is_independent_and_relocking_captures Toggling changes neither dimension, adds no undo step or preview, marks the project modified Pass same test Non-integer ratios, half-up rounding, repeated edits without drift (the naive recomputation drifts 1000 × 700 → 1000 × 697) Pass test_repeated_edits_do_not_drift, test_non_integer_ratio_repeated_edits_without_drift Presets (locked: new target; unlocked: once), Custom state, one-step undo restoring the ratio, atomic Swap inverting the target Pass test_presets_set_the_target_when_locked, test_presets_apply_once_when_unlocked, test_swap_is_atomic_and_inverts_the_target Limits and invalid input: linked dimension outside 16–8000 px refuses the whole edit, restores the pair, explains (panel and status bar); invalid text ignored Pass test_limits_reject_the_whole_edit, test_limits_reject_the_edit_and_explain No recursive signals or duplicate updates: one request, one frame update, one scene revision (preview trigger) per edit Pass test_one_request_one_refresh_per_edit (this also removed two to three redundant revision bumps per size change caused by camera notifications) Composition kept when only the resolution changes (camera, roll, pan, zoom, blue frame) Pass test_resolution_change_keeps_the_composition Persistence and compatibility: lock state and ratio in output (optional keys, schema stays 5); 0.1.0 projects open locked to their own ratio; a ratio that does not fit the size is replaced Pass test_lock_state_in_projects_and_old_files, test_lock_state_is_saved_and_restored, test_old_projects_open_locked_to_their_own_ratio GUI on the Mint display: button states, linked/unlocked edits, Custom, blue frame ratio (725 × 604 px frame for 2880 × 2400) Pass (scripted) artifacts/aspect/window-unlocked.png Hands-on use by a person (mouse and keyboard in the Render tab) Unverified

Design: one pure module (ycrystal.core.aspect) does the arithmetic; the panel emits one complete request per edit (width, height, target ratio) and refreshes its controls under QSignalBlocker; the window applies it through the existing undo command, which now also restores the target ratio. Toggling the lock is not an undo step.

Regression runs: pytest -m "not povray" 306 passed (strict mode); pytest -m povray on test_gui_render.py, test_release.py, test_gui.py 9 passed (output frame, framing gate, release workflow); doctests; zensical build --clean --strict; pre-commit on the changed files. One existing test (test_save_and_reopen_after_source_file_is_moved) typed an independent 900 × 500 size with the spin boxes; with the new locked default it now unlocks first, and it also checks that the lock state is restored.

items.title: FR-COLOR-01: explicit colour entry and colour names (post-0.1.0, 15 November 2026)
items.text:
New development after the 0.1.0 baseline (not part of M0–M6); branch feature/color-input-names. Purpose: reproducible element colours without visual matching, and colours identifiable by text. An audit against the written requirement found and fixed: three bare numbers ≤ 1 and HSV/HSL percentages were silently read as fractions; hue ran to 360 with whole-number HSV/HSL (rounding up to two channel steps); greys lost their hue; OK accepted unapplied invalid text; named-colour and spectrum texts lacked RGB values; exact named colours were labelled "nearest"; the named-colour grid had no keyboard access; no note when a material hides the colour.

Acceptance item Result Evidence 1. RGB (255, 0, 0), HEX #FF0000, HSV (0°, 100%, 100%), HSL (0°, 100%, 50%), and red give the same colour; black, white, grey, custom colours, range ends (hue 359), round trips Pass test_five_notations_give_the_same_red, test_boundaries_and_custom_colours, test_each_representation_sets_the_same_dialog_colour; repeated HSV↔HSL↔hex switching over 4,096 colours stays within one 8-bit step (test_representation_round_trips_stay_within_one_channel); integers are 0–255 and decimals 0–1, never guessed (test_numbers_are_never_reinterpreted) 2. Hover/focus texts: named swatch and element colour cell show name, HEX, RGB; spectrum hover updates per location without assigning; non-catalogue colours get exact values plus an explicitly approximate name Pass test_named_swatch_tooltip_text (red — #FF0000 — RGB (255, 0, 0)), test_colour_buttons_name_their_colour_and_use_the_dialog, test_spectrum_hover_does_not_assign, test_label_combines_description_and_name (exact vs nearest) 3. Keyboard-only editing and selection; invalid entries cannot be accepted; Cancel restores; one undo step Pass test_keyboard_only_selection_and_names, test_invalid_text_blocks_ok, test_cancel_undo_persistence_and_export 4. Scene, live viewport, .pov export, reopened project, and imported style keep the base colour Pass same test: geometry colour, Ycr_sRGB(…) in the export, project and style values identical 5. Coordinates, radius, material, opacity unchanged by colour edits; own-pigment materials explained Pass same test; test_colour_note_for_materials_with_own_pigment Bug reported on the Mint desktop: the dialog took the element's colour as background Fixed The colour button's style sheet was unscoped and cascaded into the dialog (its child). Now scoped to QPushButton#colorButton, and the dialog is parented to the window; test_dialog_does_not_take_the_button_colour Manual Appearance check on the Mint desktop (numeric entry, hover/focus texts, keyboard, Cancel/Undo, restoration) Unverified Needs a person; the automated GUI tests ran on the Mint display

Unchanged by design: the plain colour descriptions (vocabulary and rules) approved by the project owner. The colour model is the existing sRGB 0–1 triple in SceneSettings (no schema change; 0.1.0 projects open unchanged). Tests: 51 conversion and 14 dialog/GUI tests. Caveats: descriptions are English only and approximate; nearest names use CIEDE2000 (sRGB, D65); no screen colour picker; the spectrum itself has no keyboard navigation (the fields and the named-colour grid do).

items.title: M6 acceptance evidence
items.text:
Gate: a clean-install demonstration using only documented instructions, a reproducible example project/render, and a release checklist distinguishing passed, failed, and unverified items; release artifacts prepared. The full checklist is in Release procedure and checklist.

Check Result How Clean install with the documented commands Pass Fresh directory: gh repo clone, /usr/bin/python3 -m venv .venv, pip install -e . -c constraints.txt (42 s, warm pip cache), ycrystal --version → 0.1.0, --check-renderer → PASS (0.14 px), example --render (1.8 s), --export-pov, rejection of ibrav = 2 (exit 1), GUI start (running after 10 s, no errors) Documented HTTPS clone Fail while private Needs credentials; gh repo clone and SSH documented Linux Mint launcher Pass (files); menu unverified ycrystal --install-desktop writes launcher, SVG icon, and .ycrystal MIME type for the user; desktop-file-validate silent; --uninstall-desktop removes them; appearance in the Cinnamon menu needs a person Reproducible examples Pass examples/ (3 projects, 1 style; generated by scripts/make_examples.py, no machine paths); ycrystal FILE --render OUT.png without a window; each renders in 1–2 s at 400 × 300; tests render all examples End-to-end workflow (plan, section 10) Pass (automated on the Mint display) test_release_workflow: CIF → rotate/pan → 2 × 2 × 2 → Ti glossy → white studio → render → save → close → source deleted → reopen → render again (identical images), then POSCAR and QE imports, ibrav ≠ 0 rejected; a hands-on run is still recommended User guide Done New pages: examples and the command line, support matrix; install guide (checks, launcher, update, uninstall); troubleshooting (launcher) Performance on stated hardware Recorded Intel Core Ultra 5 135U, 8 GB, Meteor Lake graphics: 71 atoms 31 ms and 1,315 atoms 70 ms per drag step (unchanged from M2 despite the M4/M5 overlays); render times in the guides Review Done Constraints (pinned tested set), licences (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md: MIT with separately installed LGPL Qt/ASE; POV-Ray AGPL run as a separate program), include dependencies, known limitations Release artifacts Pass uv build: ycrystal-0.1.0.tar.gz (adds constraints, examples, fixtures, notices via MANIFEST.in) and ycrystal-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl (presets, 42 thumbnails, icon, notices); the wheel installs into a fresh environment and renders an example Tests Pass tests/test_release.py (9, including renders); 218+ non-rendering tests locally; full suite in CI

items.title: M6 caveats
items.text:
• The clean install used a warm pip cache; a first-time download (about 300 MB) was not timed.
  • The launcher's appearance in the Cinnamon menu and double-click opening of projects need a person at the desktop.
  • The end-to-end workflow was driven automatically on the real display; a hands-on run before publishing is recommended.
  • Python 3.10/3.11, Wayland, other distributions, and POV-Ray 3.8 remain unverified (see the support matrix).
  • Not tagged or published: the repository is private and publication follows the maintainer's workflow.

items.title: M5 acceptance evidence
items.text:
Gate: dragging is reversible; style reuse preserves the new structure's scientific coordinates; project round trips retain all implemented settings. The plan splits M5 into M5a (supercell handles), M5b (axis-constrained rotation), and M5c (styles and complete undo coverage).

Check Result How M5a: handles a/b/c handles (red, green, blue) outside the projected block along each periodic lattice direction; hidden without a cell, for non-periodic axes, and for directions nearly along the line of sight; View ▸ Supercell Handles toggles them (remembered); never exported test_handle_drag_adds_cells_in_one_undo_step, test_handle_drag_clamps_cancels_and_hides, test_no_handles_without_cell; screenshots in artifacts/m5/ M5a: drag Integer steps from the mouse movement projected on the lattice direction; orange outline of the new block and a label with cell and atom counts during the drag; no orbit while dragging; geometry built once on release; minimum one cell, maximum 20; Esc or right button cancels same tests (preview (3, 1, 1) before release, camera unchanged during the drag, repetitions unchanged after Esc) M5a: reversible One undo step per drag; undo/redo restore the repetitions; numeric controls follow; large expansions still ask for confirmation test_handle_drag_adds_cells_in_one_undo_step M5b: rotation modes Rotate freely (trackball, M0) or about a, b, c, x, y, z: left drag turns about the chosen axis through the view centre; the axis keeps its screen direction; a circular motion is used when the axis points at the viewer; clicks still select, Shift-drag still pans test_axis_rotation_keeps_the_axis_fixed, test_click_still_selects_in_axis_mode; Camera.rotate_about checked against an explicit Rodrigues rotation (test_rotate_about_axis_keeps_axis_fixed_on_screen) M5b: exact steps ⟲/⟳ (Ctrl+Left/Right) turn by 5–90° about the axis, or about the line of sight in free mode test_rotate_buttons_turn_by_the_step M5c: styles .ycstyle files (materials, colours, radii, display, environment, output size; no structure, no camera); parts selectable on import; one undo step tests/test_style.py, test_style_export_import_to_another_structure M5c: transfer rules Element-keyed settings and bond-pair rules transfer to elements the target contains; per-atom materials and hidden atoms only when the element sequence is identical; everything left out is explained in a message test_other_structure_gets_compatible_parts_and_explanations, test_same_structure_receives_everything Coordinates preserved Style import, handle drags, and rotation never change scientific positions assertions in the style, interaction, and docs-example tests M5c: undo coverage Every figure change is one undo step and undo restores the exact state: hiding, show all, boundary atoms, repetitions, cell mode, bonds (on/off, tolerance, radius, pairs), atom size, element radius, element colour, default/element/atom materials, clearing overrides, environment, lighting, output size; plus handle drags and style imports. Output size is now undoable (an M3 caveat); merged spin-box steps show the latest value test_every_presentation_change_is_undoable (20 operations), test_output_size_keeps_output_camera_and_marks_modified Radii Atom size (× covalent radius) in the Structure tab; per-element radius in Å in the Appearance tab; reset returns colour and radius together test_radius_controls_and_project_round_trip Project round trips Schema 5 adds element radii; overrides, colours, radii, environment, output size restored exactly; older schemas unchanged test_overrides_colours_radii_and_environment_round_trip, test_radius_controls_and_project_round_trip Verification run 218 non-rendering tests pass locally (strict mode, 62 rendering tests deselected); rendering tests were not rerun locally (M5 does not change the POV-Ray writer) to spare the laptop; CI runs the full suite pytest -m "not povray"; doctests; scripts/docs_examples.py; zensical build --clean --strict; pre-commit run --all-files

items.title: M5 caveats
items.text:
• Handles are 2D markers placed outside the projected block and clamped to the view; with a strongly tilted cell a handle can sit far from its face. Directions nearly along the line of sight have no handle until the view is rotated.
  • The view refits after a handle drag (as after numeric changes), so the block stays in the frame.
  • Esc cancels a drag through the window's Select None shortcut; without a focused window the viewport's own key handler does it.
  • Rotation modes and the step angle are navigation settings, not saved in projects and not undoable (camera navigation stays outside the undo stack by design).
  • Styles transfer per-atom settings only for identical element sequences; there is no matching of atoms between different structures.
  • Style files store the source's element sequence (one symbol per atom); for very large structures the file grows accordingly.

items.title: M4 acceptance evidence
items.text:
Gate: at least 20 materials and 12 environments render individually; representative glass/metal/sky combinations pass; style changes survive reopen; live approximations are labelled and the actual POV-Ray preview is available for effects VTK cannot show.

Check Result How Catalog size 30 materials, 12 environments, 6 lighting presets JSON manifests in src/ycrystal/presets/; test_catalog_meets_the_m4_targets Native material types All four declaration kinds (13 finish, 4 pigment, 8 texture, 5 material); 16 materials use native POV-Ray 3.7 identifiers (T_Gold_3C, F_MetalD, M_Glass, White_Marble, T_Stone25, …) with their include files; 14 have their own pigment test_writer_declares_each_material_kind, test_native_material_and_finish_identifiers; every listed include file exists in the installed povray-includes (test_manifest_fields_are_consistent) Every catalog entry renders Pass: 30 materials and 12 environments, each in its own POV-Ray 3.7 render test_every_material_renders, test_every_environment_renders (size, alpha, drawn structure, gradient for gradients and skies) Representative combinations Pass: glass/cloudy sky (blue sky above), gem/blue gradient, chrome/dark reflective studio (mirror image below), gold/dark grey, polished metal/black, marble/transparent (alpha 0), clear glass/white studio test_representative_combinations; mixed default/element/atom overrides in the grey studio (test_mixed_overrides_render_and_floor_shadows) Genuine thumbnails 42 POV-Ray thumbnails (128 × 128 px, 455 KB total) of fixed scenes; index.json records a digest of each scene, and a test fails when a recipe or the writer changes without re-rendering scripts/render_thumbnails.py (all 42 in about 34 s on the development laptop); test_every_preset_has_a_current_thumbnail; reviewed visually (artifacts/m4/) Galleries, search, favourites Pass: search by name, description, category, POV-Ray identifier, or include file; category filter; favourites in QSettings test_material_gallery_search_categories_and_favourites, test_environment_gallery_applies_preset Assignment and precedence Pass: default, element, and displayed-atom overrides (atom > element > default); half-bonds follow their atom; separate element colours; every step undoable test_material_precedence_and_colours, test_gallery_targets_apply_and_undo, test_element_table_material_and_colour, test_selection_buttons_and_edit_menu Background, floor, lighting Independent controls; a preset initialises all three. Solid, gradient, and sky backgrounds on a frame-aligned backdrop; tilted floor with shadows and optional reflection; key/fill intensities, direction, area-light size, shadows, reflection panel; spin-box drags merge into one undo step test_floor_backdrop_lights_and_reflector, test_environment_controls_merge_and_lighting_presets Transparency Transparent output leaves out floor and backdrop writer and render tests (alpha 0 at the corner) Projects Schema 4 restores overrides, colours, and the full environment exactly; schema-3 files keep their M3 appearance; unknown materials/lighting are refused with an update message test_schema4_overrides_colours_and_environment_round_trip, test_schema3_file_keeps_its_m3_appearance, test_overrides_and_environment_survive_reopen, test_render_with_overrides_after_reopen Includes in exports Header lists required include files; export warns if one is missing; render failures name the missing file and povray-includes test_export_reports_include_files, test_missing_include_is_explained Live approximations labelled One VTK actor per material; gradients and floor colours approximated; the Appearance tab states that shadows, reflections, refraction, clouds, and procedural textures appear only in the POV-Ray preview test_live_view_approximations Earlier gates unchanged M0 evidence: 0.067 px live view, 0.034 px POV-Ray; M3 gate tests pass scripts/m0_evidence.py; tests/test_gui_render.py Packaging and docs Wheel contains 30 + 12 manifests, lighting.json, 42 thumbnails, and index.json; new guide page lists every preset (checked by a test); strict docs build clean uv build --wheel; test_appearance_guide_lists_every_preset; zensical build --clean --strict Automated suite 260 passed, 0 skipped (strict mode) before the final UI/doc touch-ups; afterwards the non-rendering tests were rerun YCRYSTAL_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 pytest -q -rs; CI runs the full suite

Render times on the development laptop at preview size (480 × 320, SrTiO3 2 × 2 × 1, no antialiasing): satin on white 0.9 s, satin in the white studio 1.3 s, chrome in the dark studio 1.2 s, marble on a gradient 1.0 s, tinted glass on white 4.5 s and on the cloudy sky 5.2 s, tinted glass in the white studio (area light) 39 s.

items.title: M4 caveats
items.text:
• Transparent materials with area lights (Studio and Top lighting) are slow: POV-Ray traces filtered shadow rays through the glass (5 × 5 area samples). The guide recommends Soft/Bright lighting or switching off automatic previews while composing. The Bright preset is a point light for this reason.
  • Live view: one material per actor with Phong approximations; floors become a flat colour, skies a gradient; no shadows, reflections, refraction, clouds, or procedural patterns (labelled in the panel).
  • Native metals (T_*_3C, Polished_Chrome) keep POV-Ray's own finishes (ambient 0.1–0.35, strong reflection); on white backgrounds they look pale. Dark and studio environments with the reflection panel suit them better.
  • Procedural textures use the same pattern orientation on every atom.
  • Editable material parameters (for example a custom refractive index), user include files, and image backgrounds are not implemented (later work in the plan).
  • Floor geometry is tied to the view (below the frame, tilted 20° towards the viewer); it is not a fixed plane in crystal coordinates.
  • Material overrides refer to displayed-atom IDs, like hiding; transferring a style to another structure is M5.
  • Thumbnail digests depend on the exact scene text; a different libm could in principle change the last printed digit of a coordinate (CI and the development machine share Ubuntu 24.04's).

items.title: M3 caveats
items.text:
• Previews use full quality without antialiasing; glass, metallic reflection, and large supercells make them slower (seconds). Automatic previews are on by default and can be switched off in the preview dock (the choice is remembered).
  • POV-Ray reports progress about once per second; short renders show only 100 %. A successful render always ends at 100 % (added after a CI run whose last report was 99 %).
  • Cancel kills the POV-Ray process; nothing partial is kept.
  • The frame margin (4 %) is fixed. Output size is not undoable.
  • One material for all atoms and bonds; per-element/per-atom assignment, galleries with POV-Ray thumbnails, more presets, and lighting controls are M4.
  • python -m doctest docs/development/examples.md reports fence-line mismatches (the closing `` is read as expected output); the outputs themselves match. Pre-existing onmain`; CI does not doctest Markdown.

items.title: M2 acceptance evidence
items.text:
Gate: triclinic and hexagonal examples preserve correct geometry, stable selection, and original coordinates; expected bond/image counts; reversible repetition changes; navigation does not modify coordinates. The first increment (boundary atoms, selection, hiding, undo) is listed in the next section.

Check Result How Orthogonal SrTiO3, n × n × n (n = 1–3) Pass (n+1)³ Sr, n³ Ti, 3n²(n+1) O; 6n³ Ti–O and 12n²(n+1) Sr–O bonds; equal to a brute-force distance search over the displayed atoms; no duplicate bonds (test_supercells_bonds.py) Hexagonal MgB2, n × n × m Pass (n+1)²(m+1) Mg, 2n²m B; (3n² − 2n)·m B–B bonds (honeycomb); brute force agrees Diamond Si (conventional cell) Pass (n+1)³ + 3n²(n+1) + 4n³ atoms (18 at 1×1×1, as VESTA); 16n³ bonds, all 2.3517 Å Triclinic cell Pass 5n³ atoms at general positions; displayed bonds equal brute force for 1×1×1, 2×3×1, 2×2×2; periodic bonds unique (no reverse pairs) and complete against a search over neighbouring cells Stable IDs, reversibility, coordinates Pass Every atom of 1×1×1 has the same ID and position at 3×3×3; 1 → 3 → 1 reproduces IDs, positions, and bonds exactly; hidden IDs persist across repetition changes; structure arrays unchanged Non-periodic axes and molecules Pass No repetition along non-periodic axes; a molecule shows O–H bonds only Cell edges Pass All unit cells (grid lines), outline of the block, or the original cell; counts checked (e.g. 27 grid lines at 2×2×2) Repetition controls Pass Spin boxes a/b/c (1–20), "− all", "+ all", "1 × 1 × 1"; each change one undo step; the panel follows undo/redo; the view is refitted to the new block; selection kept by ID (test_gui_scene.py) Large-expansion warning Pass Above 20,000 displayed atoms Ycrystal asks before applying (estimate computed without building geometry); declining leaves everything unchanged Bonds panel Pass Show/hide, tolerance (× sum of covalent radii; consecutive edits merge into one undo step), radius, per-element-pair switches with per-cell counts and lengths View directions Pass a, b, c, x, y, z (Shift: opposite side); the axis points at the viewer with the next axis up (e.g. down c: a right, b up); triclinic directions follow the lattice vectors; result framed POV-Ray export Pass Bonds as half cylinders textured like their atoms; grid edges; render matches the live view (artifacts/m2/) Projects Pass Schema 2 stores repetitions, cell mode, and bond settings; schema-1 projects open with bonds off, exactly as saved Automated suite 162 passed, 0 skipped pytest -q -rs; pre-commit run --all-files clean

Display benchmark (scripts/benchmark_scene.py, SrTiO3, Intel Meteor Lake integrated graphics, Mesa 25.2.8, 1100 × 700 viewport, 8× MSAA). "Drag step" is a synthetic left-button drag through VTK's interactor with every step repainted before the next.

Cells Atoms Bonds Build (s) Load (s) Drag step (ms) Live detail 2³ 71 192 0.02* 0.16 38 40×28 spheres 6³ 1,315 4,320 0.03 0.09 72 40×28 10³ 5,631 19,200 0.07 0.22 84 24×16 14³ 14,939 51,744 0.17 0.41 88 16×10 16³ 22,065 76,800 0.26 0.50 105 16×10 20³ 42,461 148,800 0.59 0.82 150 16×10

* first call 0.49 s (one-time import of ASE's neighbour list). The live view lowers sphere and bond tessellation above 2,000 and 8,000 atoms (POV-Ray always renders exact spheres); without this, 14³ took 232 ms per step and 20³ 640 ms. The soft limit of 20,000 atoms keeps a drag step near 100 ms or less on this hardware.

items.title: M2 caveats
items.text:
• The default bond rule (1.1 × sum of covalent radii, metal–metal off in compounds) also bonds Sr–O in perovskites; switch the pair off in the Bonds panel if not wanted.
  • Bonds are drawn only between displayed atoms (no bonds to atoms beyond the boundary).
  • Each synthetic drag step costs at least ~38 ms even for tiny scenes; most of it is spent in Qt while PyVistaQt's QOpenGLWidget presents the frame. It predates M2 and is not investigated further here; VTK's own QVTKRenderWindowInteractor is the documented fallback if real interaction proves sluggish.
  • Supercell drag handles (M5), reciprocal-axis view directions, and lighting (M4, POV-Ray currently casts hard shadows) are not part of M2.

items.text:

Every result below was observed on that Mac. Linux was not re-run with these changes; the Ubuntu CI job does that when the branch is pushed.

items.title: Update: private repository (15 November 2026)
items.text: The repository was made private. pre-commit.ci is free only for public repositories, so its ci: section was removed from .pre-commit-config.yaml; hooks are now updated manually with pre-commit autoupdate (CONTRIBUTING.md). The README's CI badge was removed (it does not render for viewers without access); the static license and status badges remain. GitHub Actions and Dependabot continue unchanged (private repositories on GitHub Free have 2,000 Actions minutes per month; one CI run uses about 4). On GitHub Free, the "Protect main" ruleset is not enforced while the repository is private; it is kept for a return to public visibility. The entries above describe the setup at the time.

items.title: Documentation increment (15 November 2026)
items.text:
No runtime behavior, public signatures, or product milestone status changed. The user guide now supports M0–M2 features; this does not complete M6.

M2 was subsequently merged into main in PR #5 (49b50ec). This branch now includes that merge and documents its repetitions, periodic bonds, cell modes, view directions, and schema-2 projects. Historical checks below describe the initial increment; updated integration verification is recorded separately.

items.title: Discrepancies documented without changing behavior
items.text:
• The previous progress wording and draft GUI docstring said rendering returned immediately. In fact render_png queries the renderer version synchronously (up to 15 s) and prepares files before starting QProcess. The render itself is asynchronous. The GUI's renderer check is synchronous.
  • Frozen structure arrays do not make metadata immutable: the constructor retains the metadata dictionary, and replace shallow-copies it. Project is mutable.
  • Direct Structure construction permits occupancy up to 1 + 1e-6, does not reject non-finite coordinates/occupancies, and does not validate pbc length. The CIF reader rejects occupancy below 1 - 1e-3, rather than every value below 1. These existing tolerances/validation limits are now explicit.
  • The renderer self-test converts discovery/render failures to a result, but file preparation, image decoding, and measurement errors may propagate. A preparation failure after creating a job directory can leave partial files. GUI PNG-copy failures can leave a .part file; the GUI still removes the render job.
  • Project metadata sanitization does not recursively sanitize values converted from NumPy; non-finite values can make saving fail. Optional scene/environment/output sections default on load; missing required structure entries fail. The old M1 evidence wording “missing sections” was too broad and is clarified above.
  • core.compare.supercell is a comparison helper and accepts non-singular integer transforms, including orientation reversal; it is not a GUI supercell feature. Structure comparison wraps fractional differences component by component, rather than performing a general minimum-image search in skewed cells.

items.text:

items.text:

  • Intel Meteor Lake integrated graphics, Mesa 25.2.8, OpenGL 4.6.

items.title: Architecture decisions
items.text:
• System Python, not Miniconda. With Miniconda's interpreter, its bundled libstdc++ (GLIBCXX ≤ 3.4.29) is loaded before the system one, and Mesa 25 cannot initialise GLX: the VTK window crashed.
  • PySide6-Essentials only (no Addons/WebEngine). QT_API=pyside6 is forced before PyVistaQt/QtPy are imported.
  • Ycrystal's own POV-Ray writer from M0. ASE's exporter frames the image itself and writes camera-frame coordinates, so it cannot reproduce an arbitrary panned, non-square view. ASE remains the structure library; its exporter is a reference only.
  • Camera export: explicit location/direction/right/up vectors for an orthographic camera (no look_at, sky or angle), so POV-Ray does not re-derive the basis or change handedness. World coordinates stay right-handed in Å. #version 3.7;, no include files.
  • Colours: written as sRGB through a small macro and converted to linear light (assumed_gamma 1.0, PNG File_Gamma=sRGB).
  • Shared geometry: core.scene.build_geometry resolves atoms (stable IDs (source_atom, image)), radii, colours and cell edges once; the VTK viewport and the POV writer both consume it. Atoms are drawn with vtkGlyph3DMapper (instancing); cell edges are tubes with the same radius as the POV cylinders and cast no shadows.
  • Render jobs: per-job temporary directory, ASCII names, POV-Ray run with cwd = job directory and every output option in the job .ini (user povray.ini defaults such as Display=On cannot interfere). The PNG is then copied to the user's path. GUI renders use QProcess.
  • Renderer discovery: GUI setting → $YCRYSTAL_POVRAY → povray on PATH. --check-renderer / Render ▸ Check Renderer renders a tiny reference scene and verifies sphere positions and colours.
  • Output framing (M0, superseded in M3): M0–M2 rendered the viewport's aspect ratio. Since M3 the output size is explicit and the GUI shows the output frame.
  • Keys: VTK/PyVista default keys (e.g. q closes, w wireframe) are disabled in the viewport; application shortcuts (F = Fit, Ctrl+R = Render, Delete = hide, Esc = select none, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z = undo/redo) live on the window.
  • Boundary policy: along periodic axes atoms are wrapped into the cell (fractional tolerance 1e-3) and images on faces/edges/corners are added. A displayed atom's ID is (source atom, image offset) with position = input + offset @ cell, so IDs are stable when display settings change.
  • Hiding is presentation state: SceneSettings.hidden holds displayed-atom IDs; hidden balls are absent from the shared geometry, hence from the view and POV export. The structure is never modified (atom deletion/editing remains a later, separate feature).
  • Picking uses an analytic ray–sphere intersection with the shared camera model (core/picking.py), not VTK pickers; a click is a left press/release that moves at most 3 px. The selection highlight is a translucent shell drawn only in the live view.
  • Undo/redo: QUndoStack with one command type that swaps SceneSettings; commands with the same merge key (bond tolerance, bond radius) merge when consecutive.
  • Supercells (M2): repetitions live in SceneSettings and are always expanded from the original structure; boundary images are added on the faces of the repeated block. Image offsets stay relative to input positions, so IDs, selection, and hidden atoms are stable across repetition changes.
  • Bonds (M2): core/bonds.py searches the original cell once with ASE's neighbour list (any cell shape) and stores (i, j, integer shift) without reverse duplicates; build_geometry maps them onto displayed images and gives both renderers explicit endpoint index pairs. Rule and per-pair overrides are in BondSettings.
  • Live-view level of detail (M2): sphere/bond tessellation drops at 2,000 and 8,000 displayed atoms; bonds use the same GPU instancing (vtkGlyph3DMapper) as atoms.
  • Scene panel (M2): gui/panels/scene_panel.py emits requests only; the window turns them into undoable commands and syncs the panel with signals blocked.
  • Import (M1): ASE parses; io/readers.py adds detection, provenance (path, name, format, SHA-256, size, time, reader version, block, element mapping), and checks. Questions (format, data block, element mapping) are exceptions that the GUI answers and retries, so the readers stay GUI-free. Ycrystal's QE reader is assembled from ASE's card parsers because ASE's read_espresso_in ignores A (it looks up an upper-case key in a lower-cased namelist) and resolves labels permissively.
  • Comparison: core/compare.py compares lattice matrices directly and matches atoms by element and fractional position modulo lattice translations.
  • Projects: io/project.py, JSON schema 2 (schema 1 remains readable), written atomically; numbers are canonical, symbols are stored for readability and checked on load. Machine-specific settings (POV-Ray path, last directory) stay in QSettings, not in projects.

  • Camera notifications: the viewport now listens to the VTK camera's ModifiedEvent; the M0 observer on the interactor never fired because VTK raises EndInteractionEvent on the interactor style.

  • Output camera (M3): the GUI keeps VTK's camera for the whole view and derives the output camera (same pose, parallel scale × frame/height ratio). Export, preview, render, and projects use the output camera with the explicit output size; a render start observer keeps it fixed across window resizes.

  • Presets (M3): ycrystal.presets loads JSON manifests (declaration kind, finish, filter, interior, includes, live approximation, provenance) shipped as package data. Scenes store ids; the POV writer writes a texture or a full material per element; the viewport applies the live approximation. Background presets also set a visible cell-edge colour, changed together with the environment in one undo step.
  • Material assignment (M4): SceneSettings stores a default material plus sorted element and displayed-atom overrides and element colours; build_geometry resolves one material and colour per atom. The POV writer declares each material once per element colour (once overall for own-pigment materials) and applies unit-space textures to a scaled unit sphere. The viewport draws one actor per material.
  • Environment model (M4): Environment holds background (solid, gradient, sky), floor, lighting values, and the reflection panel; presets initialise it, the panel edits fields. Gradients and skies use a self-lit backdrop aligned with the frame (a sky_sphere would be one colour under orthographic projection) inside an empty light_group; the floor is tilted 20° towards the viewer; area lights have no jitter so renders are deterministic.
  • Lighting rig (FR-LIGHT-01): lights are values relative to the output camera (origin F, screen basis) resolved on demand by ycrystal.core.lighting; the POV writer, the live view's two scene lights, and the Lighting Setup overview consume the same rig, and no resolved positions are stored.
  • Undo model (M5): one command type carries scene settings plus optional environment and output size; handle drags, style imports, and size changes are single steps; merge keys combine spin-box edits. Camera navigation stays outside undo.
  • Styles (M5): the presentation part of the project format plus the source's element sequence; a pure apply_style returns new settings and user notes.
  • Handles and axis rotation (M5): the viewport's input filter routes handle drags and axis-mode drags away from VTK's trackball; handles are 2D overlays recomputed before each render; repetitions are applied once on release.
  • Thumbnails (M4): genuine POV-Ray renders of fixed scenes, shipped as package data, with scene digests to detect stale images.
  • Render lifecycle (M3): RenderProcess (progress, cancellation, elapsed time, completion state) and RenderQueue (one process, newest request wins, job directory removed after the result slots). The window tags previews with scene_revision and discards stale results; final renders use a separate process with Cancel.
